claims.statement: One row represents one detected signal; signalregistry is the signal's unique identifier.
One row holds the observational-conditions record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the research-process record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the advanced-phenomena record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the classification record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the decoding record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the dynamics record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the probability-scoring record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row holds the astrophysical source-properties record for exactly one signal, extending signals 1:1.
One row represents one telescope; telescregistry is the telescope's unique identifier.
One row represents one observing station/observatory; observstation is its unique identifier.
carrierfreqmhz happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key for signals is signalregistry.
centerfreqmhz happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key for signals is signalregistry.
freqmhz happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key for signals is signalregistry.

timemark happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is likely a coincidence (time-of-day stamp with fine resolution), not a designed identifier; the true row key for signals is signalregistry.
periodsec happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key is signalref.
sourcedistly happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key is signalref.
sourceradeg happens to be distinct across all 1,000 rows, but this is a coincidence of continuous measurement precision, not a designed identifier; the true row key is signalref.

The observatories table covers 963 stations, 48 of which (about 5%) have no matching row in telescopes, so equipment-level detail (status, calibration, pointing accuracy, etc.) does not exist for those stations in this database even though the station itself is recorded.

Every telescope in telescopes resolves to a real observatory in observatories (100% match); telescopes is fully contained within the observatory population, with one observatory potentially hosting more than one telescope.

Every signal row resolves to a real telescope (100% match) and has a corresponding row in every one of the eight 1:1 extension tables (observationalconditions, researchprocess, signaladvancedphenomena, signalclassification, signaldecoding, signaldynamics, signalprobabilities, sourceproperties); the signal population is fully and consistently described across these tables.

Observation dates recorded in this table run from 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 across 121 distinct months; any signal or event outside that window is simply absent from the database, and the latest date reflects when the extract was taken rather than the true end of monitoring.

Weather, seeing, lunar, solar, geomagnetic, and other atmospheric/sky-condition columns in observatories are stored once per station (the table's grain), not once per observation; they represent a single snapshot condition for the station and are not tied to the specific time any given signal was detected.

cultsig takes the assessed values High or Low; the 34.6% of rows where it is empty most likely mean cultural significance was not evaluated for that signal, not that significance is known to be absent.
discstat takes the values Full or Partial; the 32.6% of rows where it is empty most likely mean discovery status has not yet been determined, not that discovery status is absent.
encryptevid takes the values Strong or Possible; the 33.9% of rows where it is empty most likely mean this evidence was not assessed, not that no encryption evidence exists.
errcorrlvl takes the values Low, Medium, or High; the 26.5% of rows where it is empty most likely mean no error-correction scheme was recorded or applicable, not that correction level is zero.
gravlens takes the values Strong or Weak; the 33.3% of rows where it is empty most likely mean gravitational-lensing effects were not assessed, not that none occurred.
interflvl takes the values Low, Medium, or High; the 23.5% of rows where it is empty most likely mean interference level was not recorded, not that interference is zero.

langstruct takes the values Complex or Simple; the 33.5% of rows where it is empty most likely mean no linguistic structure was analyzed or found, often because the signal was not deemed message-like.
msgcontent takes the values Identified or Possible; the 30.4% of rows where it is empty most likely mean no message content was detected or assessed for that signal.
notesmemo is a free-text notes field; it is empty for 49.2% of rows simply because no note was written for that signal, not because of a data-collection failure.
quanteffects takes the values Observed or Significant; the 34.6% of rows where it is empty most likely mean no quantum effects were observed or the field was not assessed.
sigrecurr takes the values Regular or Sporadic; the 33.1% of rows where it is empty most likely mean recurrence has not been classified for that signal.

"Technosignature probability" most plausibly corresponds to the techsigprob column, a modeled probability (same real(5,4) scale as falseposprob, suggesting a 0-1 range) that a signal originates from technology; it is distinct from artsrcprob (artificial-source probability) and biosigprob (biosignature probability), which use different column precisions and may represent different scales or concepts and should not be substituted for it.

biosigprob is stored with only two decimal places (real(6,2)) unlike the four-decimal techsigprob/falseposprob columns, raising the possibility it is recorded on a percentage (0-100) scale rather than the 0-1 probability scale used elsewhere in this table; this cannot be confirmed without inspecting actual values.

natsrcprob is stored with three decimal places and a wider integer part (real(7,3)) than techsigprob, raising the possibility it is not on the same 0-1 scale as techsigprob/falseposprob; this cannot be confirmed without inspecting actual values.

artsrcprob is stored with only one decimal place (real(3,1)), unlike the four-decimal techsigprob column, suggesting it may be a coarser or differently-scaled score rather than a directly comparable 0-1 probability; this cannot be confirmed without inspecting actual values.

airtempc is a signed decimal temperature (degrees C) and legitimately takes negative values; the automated check's split into 'numeric' vs 'alphanumeric' format classes is an artifact of the minus sign not being matched by the numeric pattern, not evidence of mixed data types.
corrscore is a signed correlation-type score and legitimately takes negative values; the 'numeric' vs 'alphanumeric' format split reported is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.

doppshifthz is a signed Doppler-shift frequency value (Hz) and legitimately takes negative values (redshift/blueshift); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.

freqdrifthzs is a signed frequency-drift rate (Hz/s) and legitimately takes negative values (drifting down vs up); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.
gallat is galactic latitude in degrees and legitimately takes negative values (below the galactic plane); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.

objmag is an astronomical magnitude and legitimately takes negative values (brighter objects have lower/negative magnitude); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.
objmetal is a metallicity index (e.g. [Fe/H]-like) and legitimately takes negative values; the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.
objradvel is a radial velocity and legitimately takes negative values (approaching sources); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.

snrratio can legitimately take negative values as stored; the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types, though a negative signal-to-noise ratio may itself indicate a sub-noise-floor detection worth flagging to analysts.
sourcedecdeg is a declination in degrees and legitimately takes negative values (southern sky); the reported format split is an artifact of the minus sign, not true mixed data types.

decodemethod is a categorical column whose values are sometimes single words (e.g. FFT) and sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. Neural Network); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

decodestat is a categorical status column whose values are sometimes single words (e.g. Completed) and sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. In Progress); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

objtype is a categorical column whose values are sometimes single words (e.g. Dwarf) and sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. Main Sequence); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

peerrevstat is a categorical status column whose values are sometimes single words (e.g. Completed) and sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. In Progress); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

lunarstage is a categorical column whose values are sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. First Quarter) and sometimes single words (e.g. Full); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

weathprofile is a categorical column whose values are sometimes single words (e.g. Clear) and sometimes multi-word phrases (e.g. Partially Cloudy); the reported 'format split' simply reflects label length, not two different kinds of data.

signaladvancedphenomena records exotic/advanced-phenomena assessments for all 1,000 signals, but several of its fields (cultsig, encryptevid, gravlens, langstruct, msgcontent, quanteffects) are each null for roughly a third of rows, so comprehensive 'advanced phenomena were absent' conclusions cannot be drawn from this table for every signal.

claims.statement: One row is one account-balance snapshot record, keyed by accountbalancesnode; usertag is also unique per row (one balance snapshot per user, 1,000 users to 1,000 rows), which looks like a 1:1 user-to-balance design rather than a separate independent key.

walletsum, availsum, frozensum, margsum, realline and unrealline are continuous monetary amounts that happen to have no duplicate values in this 1,000-row table; this is a coincidence of the data volume, not evidence that any of them identifies a row (accountbalancesnode is the identifier).
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is not an independent balance and summing it together with its components double-counts.
The business term 'wallet balance' is the walletsum column, defined as the sum of available, frozen and margin sub-balances.
The business term 'margin balance' most likely refers to the margsum column, the margin component of the wallet balance, rather than the whole walletsum.
The business term 'unrealised profit and loss' is likely the unrealline column (named 'unrealized line'); its sign distinguishes gains from losses rather than a single magnitude.
unrealline holds signed values (positive and negative), consistent with recording unrealised gain (positive) versus unrealised loss (negative); it is not a pure magnitude.
realline holds signed values (positive and negative), consistent with recording realised gain versus realised loss.

The business term 'holdings' has no unambiguous column: it may refer to the market-level mkthold field here rather than to any user-level balance, since no column is explicitly named for user holdings.
One row is one analytics-indicator snapshot, keyed by analyticsindicatorsnode, linked 1:1 to a marketdata row (via mdataref) and a marketstats row (via mstatsref).
One row is one market-data (order-book depth) snapshot, keyed by marketdatanode.
One row is one market-statistics snapshot, keyed by marketstatsmark, linked 1:1 to a marketdata row via mdlink.

circtotal, highspotday, lowspotday, maxsupply, mktsize, openstake, tnoverday, totsupply, volday and vwapday all show as unique across the 1,000-row table, but this is coincidental to their being continuous numeric measures; marketstatsmark is the identifying column, not these.
fundrate is a signed funding rate (positive and negative values occur), consistent with the standard perpetual-futures convention where the sign indicates whether longs pay shorts or vice versa.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change (both positive and negative values occur), representing price increase vs. decrease over the day.
fundspot stores a timestamp of the funding-rate snapshot (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46'), not a price value, despite the 'spot' naming convention also used elsewhere in the schema.
One row is one fee charge, keyed by feesnode; a given order can have more than one fee row (fees.orderslink is many-to-one to orders).
feetotal appearing unique across all 1,000 rows is coincidental (it is a continuous monetary amount), not an indication that it identifies the row.

26.6% of fee rows reference an order id (via orderslink) that does not exist in the orders table, meaning fees exist for orders that are absent from orders; an inner join between fees and orders silently drops these rows.

The business term 'trading fees' is likely the feetotal column; it appears distinct from rebtotal, which records a rebate (a credit back to the user), so 'trading fees' as feetotal probably excludes rebate adjustments unless explicitly netted.
feerange holds a small set of tier labels (Tier1-Tier4), representing a fee-tier bucket (e.g. by volume or account level) rather than a numeric fee amount.
feecoin holds the currency the fee was charged in, limited to three stablecoin-style codes (USDT, USD, USDC).
One row is one order execution (fill) event, keyed by orderexecmark; a given order can have more than one execution row (orderexecutions.ordersmark is many-to-one to orders).
fillquote and fillsum appearing unique across all 1,000 rows is coincidental (continuous monetary measures), not evidence that they identify the row.
26.6% of execution rows reference an order id (via ordersmark) that does not exist in the orders table; an inner join between orderexecutions and orders silently drops these rows.
cancelnote holds a cancellation reason code (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null/empty value (24.4% of rows) means the execution was not cancelled, not that the reason is unknown.
exectune classifies a fill as Maker or Taker; a null value (31.1% of rows) means the execution has not been classified this way, likely because it was not actually filled.

The business term 'notional value of fills' is most likely the orderexecutions.fillsum column (notional of each individual fill), distinct from orders.notionsum which represents the notional of the whole order including any unfilled portion.
fillsum is probably fillcount multiplied by fillquote (fill quantity times fill price), though this has not been verified by a direct arithmetic check.
One row is one order; orderspivot is the surrogate primary key and recordvault is the natural key used by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin to reference the order.
dealquote and notionsum appearing unique across all 733 rows is coincidental (continuous price/notional measures), not evidence that they identify the row.

userlink, createspot, clientmark and orderstamp are each unique across all 733 order rows, meaning in this data no user has more than one order and no two orders share a creation timestamp or client reference; this may be an artifact of the sample rather than an enforced business rule.

The orders table (733 rows) is missing about 26.6% of the order ids that fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin reference, suggesting it is a partial extract (e.g. a time-bounded or filtered snapshot) rather than the full population of orders that have fee, execution or risk records.
dealedge holds the trade direction, Buy or Sell, with no other values observed.

orderflow holds order lifecycle status limited to New, PartiallyFilled and Filled; there is no distinct 'Cancelled' or 'Rejected' status here, even though orderexecutions.cancelnote separately records cancellation reasons.
ordertune holds the order type: Market, Limit, Stop or StopLimit.
timespan holds a time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, GTC or IOC.
orderbase holds the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot or API.
mktnote holds the traded instrument/market pair (e.g. 'ADA-USDC', 'ETH-USD'), limited to 12 observed pairs across BTC, ETH, ADA, SOL against USD, USDT, USDC.
notionsum is probably dealquote multiplied by dealcount (price times quantity), though this has not been verified by a direct arithmetic check.
One row is one risk/margin profile record, keyed by riskandmarginpivot, associated with at most one order via ordervault.
26.6% of riskandmargin rows reference an order id (via ordervault) that does not exist in the orders table; an inner join between riskandmargin and orders silently drops these rows.
One row is one system-monitoring snapshot, keyed by systemmonitoringpivot, linked 1:1 to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
wsstate holds the websocket connection state at the time of the monitoring snapshot: Connected or Disconnected.
mkteffect is a signed value (both positive and negative occur), consistent with recording the direction of a market-impact effect rather than only its magnitude.
slipratio is a signed value (both positive and negative occur), consistent with recording slippage direction (favourable vs. unfavourable) rather than only magnitude.
priceeffect, named analogously to mkteffect, likely also holds a signed value indicating the direction of a price impact, though this has not been directly checked.
One row is one user, keyed by usersnode, with userstamp as the natural key referenced by accountbalances and orders.

267 of the 1,000 users (26.7%) are never referenced by orders.userlink, meaning the orders table has no record of any order for them; this may mean they placed no orders, or simply that their orders are outside the orders table's scope (consistent with the orders table appearing to be a partial extract).
acctscope holds the account/product scope a user trades under: Spot, Futures, Options or Margin.

marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators and systemmonitoring have no foreign key to orders or users; market-level snapshots in these tables cannot be attributed to a specific order, trade, or user within this schema.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON blob of sentiment/flow sub-metrics (e.g. 'instflow') rather than a single scalar value; grouping or filtering on the raw string will treat near-identical JSON payloads as different categories.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON blob of order-book depth sub-fields (e.g. 'askdepth') rather than a single scalar value; grouping or filtering on the raw string will treat near-identical JSON payloads as different categories.

claims.statement: One row represents one account balance snapshot, and the table is one-to-one with users via usertag.
One row represents one analytics-indicator snapshot, linked one-to-one to a single marketdata record and a single marketstats record.
One row represents one fee (and possibly rebate) event, generally tied to a single order.
One row represents one market-data snapshot.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot.
One row represents one order execution/fill event, tied to an order.
One row represents one order; recordvault, orderstamp and clientmark are equally unique alternate identifiers for the same order.
One row represents one risk/margin profile snapshot, tied to an order.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to an analytics-indicator snapshot.
One row represents one user account.

The orders table holds only 733 orders and covers only 733 of the 1,000 users; 267 users have no order in this table, so absence of a user here does not mean they placed no orders, only that none are recorded. In addition, fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin reference order ids that do not exist in this table for about 26.6% of their rows, indicating the orders table itself is missing roughly a quarter of the orders that generated fees, executions, or risk records elsewhere.
About 26.6% of fee rows reference an order id that is absent from the orders table, so a join of fees to orders silently drops these fee records.
About 26.6% of execution rows reference an order id that is absent from the orders table, so a join of orderexecutions to orders silently drops these execution records.
About 26.6% of risk/margin rows reference an order id that is absent from the orders table, so a join of riskandmargin to orders silently drops these records.
Holds a fixed set of account-type/segment codes: Spot, Futures, Options, Margin.
Encodes the trade direction of the order, either Buy or Sell.
Encodes the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
Encodes the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
Encodes the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
Encodes the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
Identifies the currency the fee was charged in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
Identifies a fee tier bucket (Tier1-Tier4) rather than a numeric range.
Records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); empty/null means the execution was not cancelled, not that the reason is unknown.
Records the liquidity role of the fill (Maker or Taker); empty/null likely means the order was not (yet) executed.
Indicates the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
Despite its name, this column stores timestamp strings (only 8 distinct values observed), not a numeric funding-rate spot price.

A signed profit-and-loss value where negative numbers represent unrealized losses and positive numbers represent unrealized gains; the apparent 'two formats' are just negative vs. positive numbers, not two different kinds of data.

A signed realized profit-and-loss value where negative numbers represent realized losses and positive numbers represent realized gains; the 'two formats' flagged by automated checks are simply negative vs. positive numbers.
A signed funding rate; negative values are a valid and meaningful sign (direction of funding payment), not a different data type from positive values.
A signed daily price-change value; negative values indicate a price decline and positive values a price rise.
A signed market-impact value where sign indicates the direction of the effect; the two 'formats' detected are negative vs. positive numbers.
A signed slippage-ratio value where sign indicates favorable vs. unfavorable slippage; the two 'formats' detected are negative vs. positive numbers.
Stores a JSON-structured text blob of nested sentiment/flow metrics rather than a single atomic value; grouping or comparing on the raw string will not correctly aggregate equivalent records.
Stores a JSON-structured text blob of nested bid/ask depth metrics rather than a single atomic value; grouping or comparing on the raw string will not correctly aggregate equivalent records.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; summing walletsum together with any of its components double counts.
"Wallet balance" refers to accountbalances.walletsum, the total of a user's available, frozen, and margin sub-balances combined; it is not an independently held figure.
"Margin balance" most plausibly refers to accountbalances.margsum, the margin-designated portion of the wallet balance; it excludes the available and frozen portions.

"Holdings" has no per-user column in this schema; the closest match is marketstats.mkthold, which is a market/instrument-level holdings metric, not a user's personal holdings, so the term likely cannot be answered at the user level from this data.

"Unrealised profit and loss" refers to accountbalances.unrealline, a signed value where negative denotes an unrealized loss and positive an unrealized gain; it does not include realized P&L (accountbalances.realline is separate).
"Trading fees" refers to fees.feetotal, the fee charged; it excludes fees.rebtotal, which is a rebate (credit) rather than a charge and should not be summed together with fees.

"Notional value of fills" most plausibly refers to orderexecutions.fillsum, the notional value of the executed/filled quantity, which is narrower than orders.notionsum, the notional value of the order as originally placed.

claims.statement: One row represents one account balance snapshot, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode; since accountbalances joins 1:1 to users via usertag, this is effectively one row per user.
One row represents one user account, uniquely identified by usersnode, with userstamp as the natural key referenced by other tables.
One row represents one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot, with recordvault as the natural key used by other tables to reference the order.
One row represents one fee charge event, uniquely identified by feesnode, linked many-to-one to an order via orderslink.
One row represents one order execution (fill event), uniquely identified by orderexecmark, linked many-to-one to an order via ordersmark.
One row represents one risk/margin profile record, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot, linked many-to-one to an order via ordervault.
One row represents one market data snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
One row represents one market statistics snapshot, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark, joined 1:1 to a marketdata snapshot via mdlink.

One row represents one analytics snapshot combining a market data and market stats snapshot, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode, with mdataref and mstatsref each matching 100% of populated rows.
One row represents one system monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot, joined 1:1 to an analytics snapshot via aitrack.

The orders table holds only 733 orders, while fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each hold 1,000 rows and reference order ids via orderslink/ordersmark/ordervault; 26.6% of those references (266 rows, sharing the same missing id example 'OB101796') point to orders that do not exist in this table. The orders table therefore silently omits a meaningful share of the orders that fee, execution, and risk records refer to.

267 of the 1,000 users in the users table are never referenced by any row in orders, meaning the data covers accounts that have placed no recorded orders; absence of order rows for a user should be read as 'no order recorded', not 'user is inactive'.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; summing walletsum together with any of its three components double counts.
The business term 'margin balance' corresponds to accountbalances.margsum, one of the three components that sum to wallet balance (walletsum).

The business term 'unrealised profit and loss' corresponds to accountbalances.unrealline, a signed value that can be positive (profit) or negative (loss); it is distinct from realline, which is realized profit and loss.

The business term 'trading fees' corresponds to fees.feetotal, the fee amount charged per fee record, denominated in the currency given by feecoin; it is distinct from rebtotal, which is a rebate rather than a fee.

The business term 'notional value of fills' most plausibly corresponds to orderexecutions.fillsum (the value of a fill), as distinct from orders.notionsum which may instead represent the notional of the whole order rather than of individual fills; this mapping is not confirmed by any arithmetic check.

The business term 'holdings' has no confirmed single-column mapping; marketstats.mkthold is a plausible but unverified candidate, and it may instead refer to accountbalances.walletsum (wallet balance) depending on context.
acctscope holds the account's trading product type: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.

cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested) and is empty/null for executions that were not cancelled (24.4% of rows); it is not a general-purpose note field.

exectune marks whether a fill was a Taker or Maker execution; it is empty/null for 31.1% of rows, which should be treated as unknown/not applicable rather than a third category even though it groups as 'None'.
feecoin holds the settlement currency of the fee: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange holds the fee tier applied to the trade (Tier1 through Tier4), presumably based on volume or account level.
dealedge holds the order side: Buy or Sell.

orderflow holds the order's execution status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled. There is no 'Cancelled' status value here even though orderexecutions.cancelnote records cancellations, so the two tables use different status vocabularies for similar lifecycle events.
ordertune holds the order type: StopLimit, Stop, Market, or Limit.
timespan holds the order's time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, GTC, or IOC.
orderbase holds the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote holds the traded market/trading pair symbol, e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD, limited to a small fixed set of pairs across BTC, ETH, ADA, SOL versus USD/USDT/USDC.
wsstate holds the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot holds a timestamp marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken, despite its declared short text length; values span 8 distinct hourly timestamps on 2025-02-19.

fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate that can be negative as well as positive/zero; the automated check's split into 'numeric' and 'alphanumeric' format classes is an artifact of negative signs, not two genuinely different kinds of value.
mkteffect is a signed numeric measure of market impact that can be negative, zero, or positive; the reported 'format classes' reflect the presence of a minus sign, not distinct data types.
priceshiftday is a signed decimal measure of the day's price change that can be negative or positive; the two 'format classes' found are both decimal numbers differing only by sign.
realline is a signed decimal realized profit-and-loss figure that can be negative (loss) or positive (profit); the two reported 'format classes' both hold decimal numbers and differ only by sign.
slipratio is a signed decimal slippage ratio that can be negative or positive; the two reported 'format classes' both hold decimal numbers and differ only by sign.

unrealline is a signed decimal unrealized profit-and-loss figure that can be negative (unrealized loss) or positive (unrealized gain); the two reported 'format classes' both hold decimal numbers and differ only by sign.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON document (e.g. nested 'flow'/'instflow' fields) rather than a simple categorical or scalar value; the many 'variant spellings' found by the automated check are an artifact of comma-splitting JSON text, not genuine duplicate categories.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON document (e.g. nested 'depth'/'askdepth' fields) rather than a simple categorical or scalar value; the many 'variant spellings' found by the automated check are an artifact of comma-splitting JSON text, not genuine duplicate categories.
Fee records include some (26.6%) that reference orders not present in the orders table, so joining fees to orders to compute total trading fees per order will silently drop those fee rows.

Order execution records include some (26.6%) that reference orders not present in the orders table, so joining orderexecutions to orders to compute fill totals per order will silently drop those execution rows.
Risk/margin profile records include some (26.6%) that reference orders not present in the orders table, so joining riskandmargin to orders will silently drop those rows.

claims.statement: accountbalancesnode is the primary key; one row represents one account-balance snapshot.
accountbalances has exactly one row per user (usertag is unique and matches 100% of users), so it is a 1:1 extension of the users table, not a time series of balances.
availsum, frozensum, margsum, realline, unrealline and walletsum being flagged as row-unique is coincidental (they are continuous decimal measures), not evidence that they identify rows.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is defined as availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is a derived total, so adding it to its components double counts.
Margin balance corresponds to margsum, which is only the margin-reserved component of the wallet balance, not the whole wallet balance.

The term 'holdings' has no dedicated column; it most plausibly maps to walletsum (total of available, frozen and margin balances), but could be confused with market-level size columns in marketstats (mktsize, circtotal, mkthold). Analysts should confirm which is meant.
Unrealised profit and loss maps to unrealline, which is kept separate from, and is not a component of, walletsum (walletsum = availsum+frozensum+margsum only).

realline stores a signed decimal (realised P&L), which can be negative or positive; the two 'format classes' found by automated checks are an artifact of the minus sign being parsed separately, not a true mix of data types.
unrealline stores a signed decimal (unrealised P&L); the apparent two-format split reported by automated checks is caused by negative values, not by genuinely different kinds of data.
fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure that can be negative or positive; the two format classes flagged are a sign-parsing artifact, not two distinct kinds of value.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure; the two reported format classes reflect the presence/absence of a minus sign rather than a true type split.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact score; the two format classes reported are a sign-parsing artifact, not a real mix of value kinds.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio that can be negative (favorable) or positive (unfavorable); the two reported format classes are a sign artifact.
marketstatsmark is the primary key; one row represents one market statistics snapshot.

circtotal, highspotday, lowspotday, maxsupply, mktsize, openstake, tnoverday, totsupply, volday and vwapday being flagged row-unique is coincidental, since they are continuous market measures, not identifiers.
fundspot holds only 8 distinct timestamp values across 1,000 rows, indicating funding snapshots are bucketed into coarse (hourly) time slots shared by many rows rather than one unique time per row.

marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators and systemmonitoring are chained 1:1 (mdlink, mdataref, mstatsref, aitrack each match 100% and are unique), so they represent facets of the same 1,000 underlying market snapshots rather than independent populations.
marketdatanode is the primary key; one row represents one market data snapshot.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON blob of order-book depth sub-fields (e.g. askdepth) rather than an atomic value; its row-uniqueness is a side effect of the composite content, and grouping by a leading substring splits records that belong to the same underlying snapshot family.
analyticsindicatorsnode is the primary key; one row represents one analytics-indicator snapshot.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON blob of multiple sentiment sub-metrics (e.g. flow.instflow) rather than a single categorical value; row-uniqueness reflects composite content, not design intent as an identifier.
systemmonitoringpivot is the primary key; one row represents one system monitoring snapshot, linked 1:1 to an analyticsindicators record.
wsstate records the websocket connection state of a monitoring snapshot: Connected or Disconnected.
feesnode is the primary key; one row represents one fee (and possible rebate) charge, generally tied to an order.
feetotal being flagged row-unique is coincidental (it is a continuous decimal fee amount), not an identifier.
feecoin records the currency the fee was paid in: USDT, USD or USDC.
feerange holds a fee-tier label (Tier1-Tier4) applied to the trade.
Trading fees refers to feetotal, the gross fee charged; rebtotal is a separate rebate/credit figure and is not already netted out of feetotal.
26.6% of fees rows (266 of 1,000) reference an order id (orderslink) that does not exist in orders, e.g. 'OB101796'; an inner join to orders silently drops these fee records.

26.6% of orderexecutions rows (266 of 1,000) reference an order id (ordersmark) absent from orders, the same missing ids as in fees (e.g. 'OB101796'); joining to orders silently drops these execution records.

26.6% of riskandmargin rows (266 of 1,000) reference an order id (ordervault) absent from orders, the same missing ids as in fees and orderexecutions; joining to orders silently drops these risk/margin records.

orders holds only 733 order records while fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin each carry 1,000 rows referencing order ids, about 26.6% of which (the same 266 ids in each satellite table) do not exist in orders. The orders table therefore omits roughly a quarter of the orders that have fee, execution, or risk records elsewhere.

orderspivot is the primary key; recordvault is the natural/business order identifier (also unique) used by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin as the foreign key target. One row represents one order.

userlink is unique across the 733 order rows, meaning in this dataset no user is recorded as having placed more than one order; this may be a data characteristic of this sample rather than a guaranteed one-order-per-user business rule.

clientmark, createspot, dealquote, notionsum and orderstamp being flagged row-unique may reflect genuine per-order identifiers (e.g. client order id, creation timestamp) or coincidental uniqueness of continuous/timestamp values; this cannot be distinguished from the checks alone.

267 of the 1,000 users in users.userstamp are never referenced by orders.userlink; for these users the absence of order rows means no orders were recorded for them, not necessarily that they never traded.
usersnode is the primary key; userstamp is the alternate unique business identifier for a user. One row represents one user.
acctscope records the account's trading segment: Spot, Futures, Options or Margin.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order: Buy or Sell.
orderflow records order lifecycle state with values New, PartiallyFilled, and Filled.
orderflow has no explicit 'Cancelled' or 'Rejected' value, even though orderexecutions.cancelnote records cancellation reasons; cancelled orders are therefore not distinguishable by orderflow alone.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was submitted: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote records the traded market/instrument symbol (e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD); 12 distinct pairs appear.
orderexecmark is the primary key; one row represents one execution/fill event, with many executions able to belong to one order.
fillquote and fillsum being flagged row-unique is coincidental (continuous decimal fill price/value fields), not evidence of designed identifiers.
exectune records the execution role: Maker or Taker; null (31.1% of rows) likely means no fill/role was recorded for that execution row.
cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); null (24.4% of rows) means the execution was not cancelled.
Notional value of fills refers to orderexecutions.fillsum, the monetary value of an individual fill, which is distinct from orders.notionsum, the notional value associated with the whole order.
riskandmarginpivot is the primary key; one row represents one risk/margin profile record associated with an order.

risk_margin_profile likely stores a composite JSON-style risk/margin profile rather than an atomic categorical value, similar in structure to other JSON-bearing columns in this schema (market_sentiment_indicators, quote_depth_snapshot); its row-uniqueness is probably a side effect of this composite content.
seqcode and lastupdnote being flagged row-unique may indicate they function as per-record sequence/log identifiers, though this cannot be confirmed from the checks alone.

claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance snapshot for a single user (wallet/available/frozen/margin amounts at a point in time).
One row represents one market-analytics/sentiment snapshot, linked to one marketdata row and one marketstats row.
One row represents one fee (and paired rebate) charge, optionally tied to one order via orderslink.
One row represents one market-depth snapshot.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot (funding, volume, supply, etc.), linked to one marketdata row.
One row represents one execution/fill event (or cancellation event) tied to one order.
One row represents one order; recordvault is the natural key used by other tables to reference the order.
One row represents one risk/margin profile record, optionally tied to one order via ordervault.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, in a one-to-one relationship with an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row represents one user account; userstamp is the natural key referenced by accountbalances and orders.

The orders table holds only 733 orders, while fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin each have 1,000 rows and reference order identifiers that only match orders.recordvault 73.4% of the time; roughly 267 order identifiers referenced by those tables are not present in orders, so fees/executions/risk records can exist for orders that cannot be found here.
267 of the 1,000 users are never referenced by any order; the users table therefore includes accounts with no recorded trading activity, and absence from orders does not mean the account was closed.
Fees rows are not all anchored to an existing order: about 26.6% reference an order id absent from the orders table, so joining fees to orders will silently drop those fee records.
Order-execution rows are not all anchored to an existing order: about 26.6% reference an order id absent from the orders table, so joining to orders will silently drop those execution records.
Risk/margin rows are not all anchored to an existing order: about 26.6% reference an order id absent from the orders table, so joining to orders will silently drop those risk records.
dealedge encodes the trade direction of the order, taking values Buy or Sell.
orderflow encodes the order's lifecycle status, with observed values New, PartiallyFilled and Filled; no explicit cancelled/rejected status is stored in this column.
cancelnote records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); an empty/null value means the execution was not cancelled, which is true for about 24.4% of rows.
exectune records the execution role, Maker or Taker; it is empty for about 31.1% of rows, presumably where the execution was not completed or the role is not applicable (e.g. cancelled orders).
feecoin denotes the currency the fee was charged in, one of USDT, USD, USDC.
feerange denotes a fee tier bucket (Tier1-Tier4), likely reflecting volume-based fee discounting.
acctscope denotes the trading account type/scope for the user: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.
wsstate denotes the websocket connectivity state of the monitored session: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot stores a funding snapshot timestamp (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46'), despite the column being declared as text(6); the declared length does not reflect actual stored values.

unrealline is a signed amount: negative values represent an unrealized loss and positive values an unrealized gain; the 'alphanumeric' vs 'numeric' split the automated check reports is just the presence or absence of a minus sign, not two different data types.

realline is a signed amount: negative values represent a realized loss and positive values a realized gain; the format split reported by the automated check reflects only the minus sign, not distinct data types.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change: negative values mean the price fell, positive values mean it rose; the two 'format classes' reported are just the sign, not different data types.
fundrate is a signed funding rate: negative values indicate a negative funding rate paid in the opposite direction; the two 'format classes' reported are just the sign, not different data types.
mkteffect is a signed score (positive or negative) measuring market impact; the two 'format classes' reported are just the sign, not different data types.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio (positive or negative) comparing executed to expected price; the two 'format classes' reported are just the sign, not different data types.
walletsum (the wallet balance) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; summing walletsum together with any of its components double counts.
notionsum is likely the order-level notional value, computed as dealquote multiplied by dealcount, though this has not been directly verified.
fillsum is likely the executed notional value of a fill, computed as fillquote multiplied by fillcount, though this has not been directly verified.
'Wallet balance' is the total of available, frozen and margin sums (availsum + frozensum + margsum); it is not an independently settable figure.
'Margin balance' corresponds to the margsum component of wallet balance only, i.e. funds committed to margin, excluding available and frozen funds.
'Holdings' most plausibly refers to marketstats.mkthold, a market-level holdings figure, rather than a user-level balance column; this mapping is uncertain given the ambiguous naming.
'Unrealised profit and loss' covers both gains and losses, since unrealline can be positive or negative; there is no separate column restricting the term to losses or gains only.
'Trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal and excludes rebates recorded separately in rebtotal; rebates are an opposite-direction credit, not part of the fee figure.

'Notional value of fills' refers to the execution-level fillsum in orderexecutions, not the order-level notionsum in orders, since 'fills' refers to individual executions which can differ from the order's original notional when an order is only partially filled.

claims.statement: One row is one account-balance snapshot; accountbalancesnode is the surrogate key for that snapshot. Since usertag is also unique across the 1,000 rows and matches users 1:1, each user appears to have exactly one balance record.
One row of orders is one order record, identified by the surrogate key orderspivot.

recordvault is the business/external order identifier (e.g. 'OB101796'); it is unique per row and is the key other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference, rather than the surrogate orderspivot.
recordvault values are fixed-width codes that are padded with trailing spaces (e.g. 'OB101796                            '); exact string matching should trim before comparing.
One row of fees is one fee (and possible rebate) assessment, optionally tied to an order via orderslink.
One row of orderexecutions is one fill/execution event, optionally tied to an order via ordersmark.
One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile entry, optionally tied to an order via ordervault.
One row of marketdata is one market-data snapshot.
One row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
One row of analyticsindicators is one analytics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot (mdataref) and a marketstats snapshot (mstatsref).
One row of systemmonitoring is one monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
One row of users is one user account; userstamp is the externally-used, unique user identifier referenced by other tables, while usersnode is an internal surrogate key.

orders holds only 733 records, while fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin each hold 1,000 rows that reference an order id, of which only 73.4% match a row in orders. The orders table therefore does not cover roughly 26.6% of the order ids referenced elsewhere in the schema, so related fee, execution and risk rows for those ids cannot be joined to order details.
fees contains fee entries for order ids that do not exist in orders (26.60% of rows), so an inner join from fees to orders silently drops those fee records.
orderexecutions contains fill records for order ids that do not exist in orders (26.60% of rows), so an inner join from orderexecutions to orders silently drops those execution records.
riskandmargin contains risk/margin profile records for order ids that do not exist in orders (26.60% of rows), so an inner join from riskandmargin to orders silently drops those records.

267 of the 1,000 users are never referenced by orders.userlink, i.e. roughly a quarter of users have placed no order recorded in this database; their absence from orders means no trading activity was recorded for them, not that the user does not exist.

cancelnote and exectune are empty for a substantial share of rows (24.4% and 31.1% respectively) because those fields only apply to executions that were cancelled or that resulted in a fill; averages or joins on these columns silently exclude the non-applicable rows.
walletsum (the 'wallet balance') is computed as availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is a derived total, not an independent balance.
'Margin balance' refers to the margsum component of wallet balance only, i.e. the portion of walletsum held as margin, not the full wallet total.
'Unrealised profit and loss' refers to accountbalances.unrealline specifically, as distinguished from realline which holds realised profit and loss.

unrealline holds signed values representing unrealised profit (positive) or loss (negative) per account; the two 'format classes' detected by automated checks are simply negative vs. non-negative numbers, not two different kinds of data.

realline holds signed values representing realised profit (positive) or loss (negative) per account, despite its declared integer type actually storing decimals; the two 'format classes' detected are just negative vs. non-negative numbers.

fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure that can be positive or negative; the two 'format classes' found by the automated check are simply positive vs. negative numbers, not genuinely different data types.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure; negative values indicate a price decrease and positive values a price increase. The 'format classes' found are sign-based, not distinct formats.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure; negative and positive values denote opposite directions of impact, and the 'format classes' found are simply its sign.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative and positive values denote the direction of slippage, and the 'format classes' found are simply its sign.
acctscope holds the trading account type a user operates: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.
cancelnote holds the reason an execution/order was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null/empty value means the execution was not cancelled.
exectune holds the liquidity role of a fill (Taker or Maker); a null/empty value means no fill occurred for that execution row.
dealedge holds the trade side of an order: Buy or Sell.
feecoin holds the currency the fee/rebate amount is denominated in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange holds a fee-tier bucket (Tier1 through Tier4) that determines the applicable feerate/rebrate.
'Trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal, the net amount charged; rebtotal is a separate rebate amount (e.g. a maker rebate) that is not included in feetotal and effectively offsets it.
mktnote holds the traded market/trading-pair symbol (e.g. BTC-USD, ADA-USDC), combining a base coin (BTC, ETH, ADA, SOL) with a quote currency (USD, USDT, USDC).
orderbase holds the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow holds the lifecycle status of an order: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
ordertune holds the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan holds the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
wsstate holds the websocket connection state of the monitored session: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot holds the timestamp of the funding-rate snapshot (observed values cluster hourly around 2025-02-19), despite the column's declared text(6) width being narrower than the stored values.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a nested JSON document of sentiment sub-metrics (e.g. an 'instflow' field) rather than a single atomic value; the many 'variant' groupings reported by automated checks reflect this JSON structure, not inconsistent spellings of one term.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a nested JSON document of order-book depth sub-metrics (e.g. an 'askdepth' field) rather than a single atomic value; the many 'variant' groupings reported by automated checks reflect this JSON structure, not inconsistent spellings of one term.

'Notional value of fills' refers to orderexecutions.fillsum, the notional amount of an individual execution/fill, which is distinct from orders.notionsum, the notional value of the order as a whole (which may span multiple fills).

'Holdings' may refer to marketstats.mkthold, a market-level holdings figure, as distinct from the user-level wallet/margin balances in accountbalances; this mapping is inferred from column naming only and is not confirmed by any check.

claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance snapshot, identified by accountbalancesnode; other columns in this table (availsum, frozensum, margsum, walletsum, realline, unrealline) also appear unique across the 1,000 rows but are continuous measures, not alternate identifiers.
usertag uniquely identifies the balance row and joins to users.userstamp for 100% of rows, meaning each of the 1,000 users has exactly one account-balance row.
One row represents one analytics snapshot, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode, linked one-to-one to a marketdata row via mdataref and to a marketstats row via mstatsref.
One row represents one fee charge event, identified by feesnode, linked many-to-one to an order via orderslink.
One row represents one market-data snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot, identified by marketstatsmark, linked one-to-one to a marketdata row via mdlink.
One row represents one execution (fill) event, identified by orderexecmark, linked many-to-one to an order via ordersmark.

One row represents one order; orderspivot is the surrogate key and recordvault is the natural key referenced by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin. Other columns (clientmark, createspot, dealquote, notionsum, orderstamp, userlink) are also unique across the 733 rows but this is coincidental high-cardinality, not a separate identifying role.
One row represents one risk/margin profile record, identified by riskandmarginpivot, linked many-to-one to an order via ordervault.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, identified by systemmonitoringpivot, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row represents one user; usersnode is the surrogate key and userstamp is the natural key referenced by accountbalances and orders.

This table holds only 733 orders, while fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each have 1,000 rows and only match an existing order about 73.4% of the time (266 unmatched rows each, pointing to the same missing order IDs). The orders table therefore appears to be a partial extract that omits roughly 26.6% of the orders known to the rest of the database.

267 of the 1,000 users (26.7%) are never referenced by orders.userlink. These users placed no order in this extract, but that absence does not prove they never traded; it only means no order row exists for them here.

fundspot only takes 8 distinct timestamp values, all on 2025-02-19 within a roughly 8-hour span, suggesting this table (and its linked marketdata/analyticsindicators snapshots) covers a single short observation window rather than a long trading history.
This table covers all 1,000 users with exactly one balance row each; it appears to be a single current-state snapshot rather than a history of balances over time.
walletsum (wallet balance) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it should not be summed alongside its components.
notionsum likely represents the notional value of the order, probably computed as dealquote (price) times dealcount (quantity), though no automated check confirms this exact formula.
fillsum likely represents the notional value of a fill, probably computed as fillcount (filled quantity) times fillquote (fill price), though no automated check confirms this exact formula.
'Wallet balance' is defined by this column and is the sum of available, frozen and margin sub-balances, not an independently stored figure.
'Margin balance' most likely corresponds to this column, one of the three components that sum to wallet balance.
'Unrealised profit and loss' corresponds to this column; it is a signed figure where negative values represent unrealised losses and positive values represent unrealised gains.
'Trading fees' corresponds to feetotal, the total fee amount charged per fee event; it is distinct from rebtotal, the rebate total, which offsets rather than constitutes the fee.

'Notional value of fills' most likely corresponds to orderexecutions.fillsum (per-fill notional), not orders.notionsum, which reflects the order's own declared notional rather than the sum of executed fills.
'Holdings' may correspond to marketstats.mkthold, but no schema documentation or check confirms this; the mapping is uncertain.

realline is a signed numeric column (realized profit/loss); negative values represent realized losses and positive values realized gains. The check's split into 'numeric' vs 'alphanumeric' classes is an artifact of its regex not treating a leading minus sign as numeric, not evidence of two different data kinds.

unrealline is a signed numeric column (unrealised profit/loss); negative values represent unrealised losses and positive values unrealised gains. The reported 'two format classes' reflects the regex misreading the minus sign, not two genuinely different kinds of value.

fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure that can be positive or negative depending on payment direction; the two 'format classes' found by the check are simply positive vs negative numbers, not distinct kinds of data.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure; the 'two format classes' found by the check reflect positive vs negative values rather than two distinct data types.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; the 'two format classes' found by the check reflect positive vs negative slippage, not two distinct data types.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact figure; the 'two format classes' found by the check reflect positive vs negative impact values, not two distinct data types.
cancelnote is a categorical cancellation-reason code (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for rows that were not cancelled, which is about 24.4% of rows.
exectune is a categorical execution-role code (Taker, Maker); it is empty for roughly 31.1% of rows, likely executions that never completed a fill.
feecoin holds the currency denomination of the fee charged: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange holds a fee-tier bucket code (Tier1 through Tier4).
acctscope holds the trading account type/segment: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.
dealedge holds the trade direction: Buy or Sell.
orderflow holds the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
ordertune holds the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan holds a time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase holds the order entry channel: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote holds the traded market pair symbol (e.g. BTC-USD, ADA-USDC), with 12 distinct pairs observed across what appear to be 4 base assets and 3 quote currencies.
wsstate holds the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.

This column stores a nested JSON payload of sentiment metrics (e.g. instflow) rather than a categorical code; the many 'variant' groupings the check found are different JSON payloads sharing a truncated prefix, not duplicate spellings of one category.

This column stores a nested JSON payload of order-book depth (e.g. askdepth) rather than a categorical code; the many 'variant' groupings the check found are different JSON payloads sharing a truncated prefix, not duplicate spellings of one category.

claims.statement: One row represents one order; orderspivot (and the alternate key recordvault) identifies a single order record, with 733 distinct orders in the table.
One row represents one user; usersnode (and the alternate key userstamp) identifies a single user record, with 1,000 distinct users.
One row represents one account-balance snapshot for one user; the table is one-to-one with users since usertag is unique and matches users.userstamp for 100% of rows.
One row represents one market-data snapshot; marketdatanode identifies a single snapshot, with 1,000 distinct snapshots, each with its own marketstats and analyticsindicators row in a 1:1 chain.
One row represents one set of market statistics tied one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot via mdlink (100% match, unique on both sides).
One row represents one analytics-indicator snapshot, linked one-to-one to both a marketdata row (mdataref) and a marketstats row (mstatsref), each matching 100%.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, tied one-to-one to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack (100% match).
One row represents one fee record, nominally one per order, though only 73.4% of the 1,000 fee rows resolve to an order actually present in the orders table.
One row represents one order-execution record, nominally one per order, though only 73.4% of the 1,000 rows resolve to an order present in the orders table.
One row represents one risk/margin profile record, nominally one per order, though only 73.4% of the 1,000 rows resolve to an order present in the orders table.

The orders table covers only 733 of the roughly 1,000 orders that are referenced by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin; about 266-267 order identifiers used elsewhere do not exist in orders, so those records cannot be joined to an order and silently drop out of an inner join.
26.6% of fee rows reference an order identifier that does not exist in orders, so these fees cannot be attributed to any order in this database.
26.6% of order-execution rows reference an order identifier that does not exist in orders, so these fills cannot be attributed to any order in this database.
26.6% of risk-and-margin rows reference an order identifier that does not exist in orders, so these risk profiles cannot be attributed to any order in this database.
267 of the 1,000 users (26.7%) have no row in orders at all; absence of an order for a user means no order was recorded for them in this database, not that the user had no trading activity elsewhere.
acctscope is a categorical account-type code with four values: Spot, Futures, Options, Margin.
cancelnote records the reason an order execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null/empty value (24.4% of rows) means the execution was not cancelled.
exectune records the liquidity role of the fill (Taker or Maker); a null/empty value (31.1% of rows) means the order had no execution/fill yet.
feecoin is the currency in which the fee amount is denominated: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange is a fee-tier label with four tiers (Tier1-Tier4), likely reflecting volume- or account-based fee discount bands.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order: Buy or Sell.
orderflow is the order lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
ordertune is the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan is the time-in-force code governing order expiry: GTC, GTD, FOK, or IOC.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote is the traded market/instrument pair, e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD, BTC-USDT, covering 12 distinct trading pairs across 4 base assets and 3 quote currencies.
wsstate is the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.

fundspot stores a full timestamp (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46') marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken, despite the column being declared as only 6 characters wide; only 8 distinct hourly timestamps appear.
fundrate holds a signed decimal funding rate; the two 'format classes' found by automated checks are an artifact of the leading minus sign on negative values, not two different kinds of data.
mkteffect holds a signed decimal market-impact measure; the two 'format classes' found are an artifact of the leading minus sign on negative values, not two different kinds of data.
priceshiftday holds a signed decimal daily price shift; the two 'format classes' found are an artifact of the leading minus sign on negative values, not two different kinds of data.
slipratio holds a signed decimal slippage ratio, which can be positive or negative; the two 'format classes' found are an artifact of the leading minus sign, not two different kinds of data.

realline holds the realized profit-and-loss amount for the account, a signed decimal (can be negative for a realized loss or positive for a realized gain) despite being declared as an integer type; the two 'format classes' found are an artifact of the sign, not two different kinds of data.

unrealline holds the unrealized profit-and-loss amount for the account, a signed decimal (negative means unrealized loss, positive means unrealized gain) despite being declared as an integer type; the two 'format classes' found are an artifact of the sign, not two different kinds of data.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON-like nested payload (e.g. containing an 'instflow' field), not an atomic category; the 'variant spellings' the checks found are simply distinct full JSON payloads sharing a common numeric prefix, not duplicate labels of the same thing.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON-like nested payload (e.g. containing an 'askdepth' field), not an atomic category; the 'variant spellings' the checks found are simply distinct full JSON payloads sharing a common numeric prefix, not duplicate labels of the same thing.
wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is not an independent quantity, so summing walletsum alongside its components double counts.
The business term 'wallet balance' refers to accountbalances.walletsum, defined as the sum of available, frozen, and margin sub-balances for a user.
The business term 'margin balance' refers to accountbalances.margsum, one of the three components summed to produce the wallet balance.

The business term 'unrealised profit and loss' refers to accountbalances.unrealline, a signed amount that can be a gain (positive) or a loss (negative) and is distinct from the realized P&L stored in realline.
The business term 'trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal, the fee amount charged on an order; it is distinct from rebtotal (a rebate) and is only linkable to an order for 73.4% of fee rows.

The business term 'notional value of fills' refers to orderexecutions.fillsum, the executed notional amount of a fill, as distinct from orders.notionsum which is the notional value stated on the order itself.
The business term 'holdings' most plausibly refers to marketstats.mkthold, a market-level holdings figure, rather than to any per-user balance column.

claims.statement: One row represents one account‑balance snapshot, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode; given the 100% 1:1 match to users via usertag, each row also corresponds to exactly one user.
One row represents one analytics-indicator snapshot, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode, linked one-to-one to a single marketdata row and a single marketstats row.
One row represents one fee charge record, uniquely identified by feesnode, optionally associated with one order.
One row represents one market-data (quote depth) snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark, linked one-to-one to a marketdata row.
One row represents one order execution (fill) event, uniquely identified by orderexecmark.
One row represents one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot (and equivalently by the natural key recordvault).
One row represents one risk/margin profile record, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot, optionally associated with one order.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators row.
One row represents one user account, uniquely identified by usersnode (and equivalently by the natural key userstamp).
Orders only holds 733 orders, and its userlink column is unique per row, so no user has more than one order recorded here; this is a subset of activity, not a full order history per user.

The orders table omits roughly 266 order identifiers that are referenced by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin (each of which has 1,000 rows); only 73.4% of those child rows match an order in this table, so orders undercounts the full set of orders that have fees, fills, or risk profiles.
26.6% of fee rows reference an order id that is not present in orders, so joining fees to orders will silently drop these rows and understate total fees.
26.6% of execution rows reference an order id not present in orders, so joining fills to orders will silently drop these rows and understate fill volume/notional.
26.6% of risk/margin rows reference an order id not present in orders, so joining risk profiles to orders will silently drop these rows.

267 of the 1,000 users are never referenced by orders.userlink, meaning the orders table reflects only 733 of the 1,000 registered users; absence of order rows for a user means no recorded order, not necessarily no activity.
marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators and systemmonitoring carry no foreign keys to orders or users; they represent market-wide/system snapshots independent of any specific trade or account.
acctscope is a categorical account-type/scope indicator with four values: Spot, Futures, Options, Margin.
dealedge records the trade side of the order: Buy or Sell.
orderflow is the order lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
ordertune is the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan is the order's time-in-force instruction: GTD, FOK, GTC, or IOC.
orderbase records the channel/platform the order was placed from: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote holds the traded market/pair symbol (e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD), with 12 distinct pairs observed.
feecoin is the currency in which the fee amount is denominated: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange is a fee tier label (Tier1-Tier4) reflecting the fee schedule applied.
wsstate records the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.

cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty/null for the 24.4% of rows where the execution was not cancelled, so missing values mean 'not cancelled', not 'unknown'.
exectune records whether the fill was Maker or Taker liquidity; it is empty for 31.1% of rows, likely where no fill (e.g. cancelled/unfilled) occurred.
fundspot stores a timestamp (the funding snapshot time), taking one of 8 distinct hourly values rather than being a free-form code.
fundrate is a signed funding-rate value; negative values indicate a negative funding rate direction, not a different data type despite the format-check splitting signed from unsigned values.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure; negative and positive values denote direction of impact, not distinct formats.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change; negative values mean the price fell over the day, positive values mean it rose.
realline is the realised profit-and-loss figure; negative values represent a realised loss, positive values a realised gain.
unrealline is the unrealised profit-and-loss figure referenced by the business term 'unrealised profit and loss'; negative values represent an unrealised loss, positive values an unrealised gain.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative and positive values indicate the direction of slippage (unfavourable vs favourable), not two different formats.
The wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; summing walletsum together with its components would double count.
notionsum is likely the notional value of the order, computed as dealcount (quantity) times dealquote (price); this is inferred from column naming only and not confirmed by any check.
fillsum is likely the notional value of a fill, computed as fillcount (quantity filled) times fillquote (fill price); this is inferred from column naming only and not confirmed by any check.
The business term 'wallet balance' refers to accountbalances.walletsum, the total of available, frozen, and margin sums.
The business term 'margin balance' refers to accountbalances.margsum, the margin-designated portion of the wallet balance, not the whole walletsum.

The business term 'holdings' is ambiguous in this schema: it may refer to accountbalances.walletsum (user wallet holdings) or to marketstats.mkthold (a market-level holdings metric); neither is confirmed as the intended referent.
The business term 'unrealised profit and loss' refers to accountbalances.unrealline, as distinguished from the similarly-named realline (realised P&L).
The business term 'trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal, the fee amount charged in the currency given by feecoin; this excludes rebtotal, which is a separate rebate amount.
The business term 'notional value of fills' refers to orderexecutions.fillsum (the notional of an individual fill), as distinct from orders.notionsum, which is the notional value of the whole order.

claims.statement: Each row is one uniquely identified detected signal record.
Each row is one uniquely identified observing station.
Each row is one telescope instrument. A single observatory (observstation) can host multiple telescopes, so joining from observatories to telescopes can multiply rows per station.
One row of observational conditions exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of research-process status exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of advanced-phenomena annotations exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of classification data exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of decoding effort data exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of signal-dynamics stability data exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of probability scores exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
One row of source-property data exists for each signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.

Observational condition records span roughly 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 (121 distinct months); observations outside that window are simply absent from the table, not represented as zero, and any apparent trend ending at the latest date is an artefact of the extract window.

The telescopes table does not cover every observatory station: 48 of 963 stations (about 5%) have no telescope recorded, so station-level analyses that join through telescopes silently drop those stations rather than showing zero instruments.
cultsig records an assessed level of cultural significance (High or Low); the 34.6% of rows left blank mean the assessment was not made, not that significance is zero.
discstat records disclosure status (Full or Partial); the 32.6% of rows left blank mean disclosure status was not determined, not that nothing was disclosed.
encryptevid records the strength of evidence of encryption (Strong or Possible); the 33.9% of rows left blank mean no assessment was recorded, not absence of encryption.
errcorrlvl records an error-correction level (Low, Medium, High); the 26.5% of rows left blank mean the level was not specified, not that no correction was applied.
gravlens records an assessed gravitational-lensing strength (Strong or Weak); the 33.3% of rows left blank mean no assessment was recorded.
interflvl records an assessed interference level (Low, Medium, High); the 23.5% of rows left blank mean interference was not assessed, not that there was none.
