claims.statement: Each row of signals is one distinct detected signal event, uniquely identified by signalregistry.
Each row of telescopes is one distinct telescope/instrument, uniquely identified by telescregistry.
Each row of observatories is one distinct observing station, uniquely identified by observstation.
Each row of observationalconditions corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of researchprocess corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of signaladvancedphenomena corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of signalclassification corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of signaldecoding corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of signaldynamics corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of signalprobabilities corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.
Each row of sourceproperties corresponds to exactly one signal in signals, identified by signalref, matching signals.signalregistry one-to-one.

signals is the central fact table of detected signals; each of its eight satellite tables (observationalconditions, researchprocess, signaladvancedphenomena, signalclassification, signaldecoding, signaldynamics, signalprobabilities, sourceproperties) extends every signal row exactly once, so joining any of them to signals omits none of the signal population.

observatories includes stations that currently have no telescope on record: 48 of 963 stations (4.98%) are never referenced by telescopes, so an inner join from observatories to telescopes silently drops these stations rather than showing them with zero telescopes.

observationalconditions' recorded observation dates run from 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 across 121 distinct months; observations outside this window are absent from the table rather than being zero, and any trend ending at 2025-02-09 reflects the extract boundary, not a real decline.

'Technosignature probability' refers specifically to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, a dedicated probability score for technological origin stored to 4 decimal places; it is a distinct measure from biosigprob (biological-origin probability), natsrcprob (natural-origin probability) and artsrcprob (artificial-source score), which are stored at different precisions/scales and should not be combined with or substituted for it.

cultsig records an assessed level of cultural significance of the signal (High or Low); it is blank in 34.6% of rows, meaning the assessment was not made or not applicable, not that significance is zero.
discstat records the discovery/disclosure status (Full or Partial); it is blank in 32.6% of rows, meaning no disclosure status has yet been determined, not that disclosure is absent.
encryptevid records evidence of encryption found in the signal (Strong or Possible); it is blank in 33.9% of rows, meaning no encryption assessment was recorded, not that no encryption exists.
errcorrlvl records the detected error-correction level (Low, Medium, High); it is blank in 26.5% of rows, meaning the characteristic was not determined for those signals.
gravlens records whether gravitational lensing effects were observed (Strong or Weak); it is blank in 33.3% of rows, meaning lensing was not assessed, not that none occurred.
interflvl records the recorded level of interference (Low, Medium, High); it is blank in 23.5% of rows, meaning interference level was not recorded, not that interference was zero.
langstruct records the assessed linguistic structure of any decoded message (Complex or Simple); it is blank in 33.5% of rows, meaning no language structure was identified or assessed.
msgcontent records whether message content was found (Identified or Possible); it is blank in 30.4% of rows, meaning no determination about message content was made for those signals.
quanteffects records observed quantum-level effects (Observed or Significant); it is blank in 34.6% of rows, meaning quantum effects were not assessed for those signals.
sigrecurr records whether the signal recurs (Regular or Sporadic); it is blank in 33.1% of rows, meaning recurrence was not determined, not that the signal is known non-recurring.
notesmemo is a free-text research note field that is empty in 49.2% of rows; an empty value means no note was written, not that there is nothing noteworthy.
sigclasstype classifies each signal's likely origin into exactly four categories: Artificial, Natural, Candidate, or Unknown; there is no finer-grained or combined category.
signalclass categorizes the waveform shape into exactly five values: Broadband, Continuous, Pulsed, Narrowband, Modulated.
objtype classifies the inferred nature of the source object into Unknown, Dwarf, Giant, or Main Sequence; 'Unknown' is a recorded category rather than a missing value.
celestobj classifies the type of celestial object associated with the signal into Galaxy, Unknown, Planet, or Star; 'Unknown' is a recorded category, not a null.
sigpattern categorizes the detected pattern into Structured, Random, Unknown, or Periodic.
modtype records the modulation type as one of five values: PM, FM, AM, Unknown, QAM.
polarmode records the polarization mode as one of four values: Linear, Unknown, Circular, Elliptical.
airtempc stores signed air temperature in Celsius, including sub-zero readings; the two 'format classes' found by automated checks are simply negative vs. non-negative numbers, not two kinds of data.

corrscore is a signed correlation score; negative values indicate anti-correlation and positive values indicate positive correlation, and the two 'format classes' flagged by automated checks are simply negative vs. non-negative numbers.

doppshifthz is a signed Doppler shift in Hz despite being declared numerically as an integer; negative values indicate a blue-shift (motion toward the observer) and positive values a red-shift (motion away), with 522 of 1,000 rows holding negative/decimal values.
freqdrifthzs is a signed frequency drift rate (Hz/s); negative values mean the signal's frequency is decreasing over time and positive values mean it is increasing.
gallat is galactic latitude in degrees; negative values lie south of the galactic plane and positive values lie north of it.
objmag is apparent magnitude, an inverse brightness scale where lower (more negative) values denote brighter objects and higher values denote fainter objects.
objmetal is a stellar metallicity index; negative values indicate metal-poor (sub-solar) composition and positive values indicate metal-rich (super-solar) composition.
objradvel is radial velocity; negative values indicate the source is approaching (blue-shifted) and positive values indicate it is receding (red-shifted).
snrratio is a signed signal-to-noise ratio; negative values (330 of 1,000 rows) indicate the detection's noise exceeded the signal rather than representing an error.
sourcedecdeg is celestial declination in degrees; negative values are in the southern celestial hemisphere and positive values are in the northern.

claims.statement: Each row of signals is one uniquely registered signal detection event.
Each row of observatories is one uniquely named observing station.
Each row of telescopes is one uniquely registered telescope/instrument.
Each row of observationalconditions is the set of observing conditions recorded for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of researchprocess is the research/publication status for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of signaladvancedphenomena is the advanced-phenomena assessment for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of signalclassification is the classification profile for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of signaldecoding is the decoding effort/result for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of signaldynamics is the dynamical/stability profile for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of signalprobabilities is the set of probability/likelihood scores for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.
Each row of sourceproperties is the astrophysical source description for exactly one signal; the table is a 1:1 extension of signals.

The table only contains observing-condition records dated between 2015-02-23 and 2025-02-09 (121 distinct months); anything outside that window is simply absent from the data, not a zero or negative observation, and an apparent decline near the end of the range may just be where the extract stops.

telescopes does not hold a record for every known observatory: 48 of the 963 observatories (about 5%) have no matching telescope row, so for those sites there is no instrument and therefore no signal data in this database, which is not the same as those sites having produced zero signals.

Cultural significance ('cultsig') is only assessed as High or Low for about two-thirds of signals; for the remaining 34.6% the field is blank, meaning the assessment was never made, not that significance is absent or zero.

Discovery status ('discstat') is recorded as Full or Partial for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 32.6% are blank, meaning discovery status has not been determined, not that discovery failed.

Evidence of encryption ('encryptevid') is recorded as Strong or Possible for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 33.9% are blank, meaning the question was not evaluated for those signals rather than evidence being absent.

Error-correction level ('errcorrlvl') is categorized as Low/Medium/High for about three-quarters of signals; the remaining 26.5% are blank, meaning the level was not determined rather than error correction being absent.
Gravitational-lensing assessment ('gravlens') is Strong or Weak for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 33.3% are blank, meaning the assessment was not made rather than lensing being absent.
Interference level ('interflvl') is categorized as Low/Medium/High for about three-quarters of signals; the remaining 23.5% are blank, meaning interference was not assessed rather than being zero.

Language structure assessment ('langstruct') is Complex or Simple for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 33.5% are blank, meaning the assessment was never made rather than structure being absent.
Message content ('msgcontent') is Identified or Possible for about 70% of signals; the remaining 30.4% are blank, meaning no assessment was recorded rather than no content existing.
notesmemo is a free-text notes field populated for only about half (50.8%) of signals; the blank half means no note was entered, not that there is definitively nothing to note.

Quantum effects assessment ('quanteffects') is Observed or Significant for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 34.6% are blank, meaning the question was not evaluated rather than effects being absent.

Signal recurrence ('sigrecurr') is categorized as Regular or Sporadic for about two-thirds of signals; the remaining 33.1% are blank, meaning recurrence was not assessed rather than the signal being a one-off.

veriflvl (verification level) takes the fixed categories Unverified, Partially, Verified.
weathprofile takes the fixed categories Clear, Cloudy, Partially Cloudy.
airtempc stores signed air-temperature values (both below and above 0°C), so a negative value means below freezing, not an error or alternate unit.
corrscore stores signed values, so its sign indicates the direction of correlation (positive vs. negative correlation), not just magnitude.

doppshifthz stores signed, fractional hertz values (e.g. -10.24, 101.96) despite its integer column type, so it should be treated as a continuous measurement whose sign indicates redshift (receding) vs. blueshift (approaching).
freqdrifthzs stores signed drift values, so the sign indicates the direction of frequency drift (increasing vs. decreasing).
gallat (galactic latitude) stores signed degree values, with sign indicating the source's position north or south of the galactic plane.
objmag (apparent magnitude) stores signed values; lower, including negative, magnitudes denote brighter objects on the standard astronomical magnitude scale.
objmetal (metallicity) stores signed values, consistent with a [Fe/H]-style scale measured relative to solar metallicity, where negative means below solar.
objradvel (radial velocity) stores signed values, with sign indicating approach (negative) vs. recession (positive) relative to the observer.
snrratio stores signed values (likely a dB scale), so negative values mean the signal is below the reference/noise level rather than being an error.
sourcedecdeg (declination) stores signed degree values, with sign indicating position north or south of the celestial equator.

The business term 'technosignature probability' refers to the techsigprob column specifically: the model's estimated probability that a signal is of technological origin, distinct from biosigprob (biological-origin probability), natsrcprob/artsrcprob (natural vs. artificial source likelihood) and anomscore/sigunique (anomaly and uniqueness scores), which capture different aspects of the signal.

claims.statement: One row of signals is one uniquely identified signal detection event.
One row of observatories is one uniquely identified observing station.
One row of telescopes is one uniquely identified telescope/instrument.
One row of observationalconditions is the observing-conditions record for exactly one signal.
One row of researchprocess is the research/process-tracking record for exactly one signal.
One row of signaladvancedphenomena is the advanced-phenomena record for exactly one signal.
One row of signalclassification is the classification record for exactly one signal.
One row of signaldecoding is the decoding-attempt record for exactly one signal.
One row of signaldynamics is the dynamics/stability record for exactly one signal.
One row of signalprobabilities is the probability/scoring record for exactly one signal.
One row of sourceproperties is the astrophysical-source record for exactly one signal.

The table's obsdate values span 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 across 121 distinct months; any date outside this window is simply absent from the extract, and the apparent end of data at 2025-02-09 reflects the extract cutoff rather than an actual stop in observations.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching observationalconditions row, so this table fully covers the signals population with no missing or duplicated observing-conditions records.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching researchprocess row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching signaladvancedphenomena row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching signalclassification row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching signaldecoding row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching signaldynamics row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching signalprobabilities row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every one of the 1,000 signals has exactly one matching sourceproperties row, so this table fully covers the signals population.
Every signal row has a telescref that matches an existing telescope, so signals never reference a telescope absent from the telescopes table.

The telescopes table does not have a row for every observatory: 48 of 963 observatories (about 5%) have no telescope recorded, so joining observatories to telescopes silently drops those observatories' instrument data rather than implying they have no telescope.
Every telescope row references an observatory that exists in observatories, so telescopes never point to a missing observatory.
airtempc records air temperature in Celsius and includes negative values (e.g. -0.2), i.e. the scale is signed around a zero point rather than a magnitude-only measure.
corrscore can take both negative and positive values (e.g. -0.003 and 0.001), indicating it encodes direction of correlation, not just a magnitude.
doppshifthz takes both negative and positive values, representing the direction of the Doppler shift (e.g. blueshift vs redshift), not a magnitude-only quantity.
freqdrifthzs takes both negative and positive values, representing the direction of frequency drift over time.
gallat (galactic latitude) takes both negative and positive values, indicating position above or below the galactic plane.
objmag (object magnitude) takes both negative and positive values, consistent with the astronomical magnitude scale where more negative values denote brighter objects.
objmetal (metallicity) takes both negative and positive values, consistent with a [Fe/H]-style scale measured relative to solar metallicity rather than an absolute magnitude.
objradvel (radial velocity) takes both negative and positive values, representing direction of motion (approaching vs receding) relative to the observer.
sourcedecdeg (declination) takes both negative and positive values, consistent with the celestial coordinate scale spanning southern and northern sky.
snrratio takes both negative and positive values, indicating signal strength can fall below as well as above the noise floor on this scale.

cultsig holds High/Low assessments of cultural significance only when an assessment was made; the 34.6% NULL/empty rows mean the signal was not evaluated for cultural significance, not that significance is zero.
encryptevid holds Strong/Possible assessments of encryption evidence only when evaluated; the 33.9% NULL/empty rows mean no such assessment was recorded for that signal.
gravlens holds Strong/Weak assessments of gravitational lensing only when evaluated; the 33.3% NULL/empty rows mean no assessment was recorded, not absence of lensing.
langstruct holds Complex/Simple assessments of apparent linguistic structure only when evaluated; the 33.5% NULL/empty rows mean no such assessment exists for that signal.
msgcontent holds Identified/Possible assessments of message content only when evaluated; the 30.4% NULL/empty rows mean no determination was made, not that no message exists.
quanteffects holds Observed/Significant assessments of quantum effects only when evaluated; the 34.6% NULL/empty rows mean no assessment was recorded for that signal.
discstat holds Full/Partial disclosure status only when a disclosure determination has been made; the 32.6% NULL/empty rows mean no determination has been recorded for that signal.
errcorrlvl holds Low/High/Medium error-correction levels only when the decoding process recorded one; the 26.5% NULL/empty rows mean no error-correction level was recorded.
sigrecurr holds Regular/Sporadic recurrence assessments only when evaluated; the 33.1% NULL/empty rows mean recurrence was not assessed for that signal.

interflvl holds Medium/Low/High interference-level assessments only when recorded; the 23.5% NULL/empty rows mean interference level was not assessed for that signal, not that interference was absent.
notesmemo is a free-text memo field that is empty for 49.2% of signals, meaning most signals have no analyst notes recorded rather than notes stating 'none'.

"Technosignature probability" refers to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, a modeled likelihood (stored as a fractional real value) that a given signal originates from technological activity, as distinct from natsrcprob (natural origin), biosigprob (biological origin), and artsrcprob (artificial source) probabilities stored in the same table.

claims.statement: One row of signals is one distinct detected signal, uniquely identified by signalregistry.
One row of observationalconditions is the observational-conditions record for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of researchprocess is the research-process status for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of signaladvancedphenomena is the advanced-phenomena assessment for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of signalclassification is the classification record for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of signaldecoding is the decoding attempt/record for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of signaldynamics is the dynamics/stability assessment for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of signalprobabilities is the probability-scoring record for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of sourceproperties is the source-characterization record for exactly one signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row of observatories is one observing station, uniquely identified by observstation.
One row of telescopes is one telescope, uniquely identified by telescregistry, with each telescope belonging to exactly one observatory.
Every telescope row references an observatory that exists in observatories; the telescopes table does not contain orphaned station references.

48 of 963 observatories (about 5%) have no telescope recorded against them in telescopes; for these stations the database has no telescope-level equipment, calibration, or operational data, which is an absence of recording rather than evidence that no telescope exists there.

Recorded observation dates span 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 across 121 distinct months; any analysis is limited to this window, and anything outside it is simply absent from the extract rather than a true zero, so apparent trends near the end date may just reflect the extract cutoff.

cultsig is a three-level category (High/Low/blank) where the blank/null state (34.6% of rows, about as common as either named level) likely represents a genuine 'not assessed' or 'none' outcome rather than random missing data.

encryptevid is a three-level category (Strong/Possible/blank) where the blank/null state (33.9% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no evidence' outcome rather than random missing data.

gravlens is a three-level category (Strong/Weak/blank) where the blank/null state (33.3% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no lensing' outcome rather than random missing data.

langstruct is a three-level category (Complex/Simple/blank) where the blank/null state (33.5% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no structure detected' outcome rather than random missing data.

msgcontent is a three-level category (Identified/Possible/blank) where the blank/null state (30.4% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no message content' outcome rather than random missing data.

quanteffects is a three-level category (Observed/Significant/blank) where the blank/null state (34.6% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no quantum effects' outcome rather than random missing data.

discstat is a three-level category (Full/Partial/blank) where the blank/null state (32.6% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no disclosure' outcome rather than random missing data.

sigrecurr is a three-level category (Regular/Sporadic/blank) where the blank/null state (33.1% of rows, comparable in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no recurrence observed' outcome rather than random missing data.

errcorrlvl is a four-level category (Low/High/Medium/blank) where the blank/null state (26.5% of rows, similar in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no error correction applied' outcome rather than random missing data.

interflvl is a four-level category (Medium/Low/High/blank) where the blank/null state (23.5% of rows, similar in size to the named levels) likely represents a genuine 'no interference assessed' outcome rather than random missing data.

The business term 'technosignature probability' corresponds to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, the modeled probability that a signal is of technological origin; it is a distinct quantity from artsrcprob (artificial-source probability), biosigprob (biosignature probability), and natsrcprob (natural-source probability), which capture related but different origin assessments and should not be substituted for it.

claims.statement: Each row of signals is one distinct detected signal event, uniquely identified by signalregistry.
Each row of telescopes is one distinct telescope, uniquely identified by telescregistry.
Each row of observatories is one distinct observatory/station, uniquely identified by observstation.
observationalconditions holds one row per signal, recording the observing conditions for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
researchprocess holds one row per signal, recording the research/publication pipeline status for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
signaladvancedphenomena holds one row per signal, recording exotic/advanced phenomena attributes for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
signalclassification holds one row per signal, recording the classification outcome for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
signaldecoding holds one row per signal, recording the decoding effort and outcome for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
signaldynamics holds one row per signal, recording the temporal/spectral stability attributes for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
signalprobabilities holds one row per signal, recording the various probability/likelihood scores for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.
sourceproperties holds one row per signal, recording the putative source's astrophysical properties for that signal as a 1:1 extension of signals.

Observation records span 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 (121 distinct months); since observationalconditions is a 1:1 extension of signals, this is also the effective temporal coverage of the signals table, and anything outside that window is absent rather than recorded as zero or null activity.

48 of the 963 observatories (about 5%) are never referenced by any row in telescopes, so any analysis that reaches observatories only by joining from telescopes silently omits these stations and all signals that might otherwise be attributed to them.

Every telescope's observstation value matches an existing observatories row (100% of 949 telescopes), so telescopes carries no orphaned observatory references and is fully covered going telescope-to-observatory.

Several exotic-phenomena columns (cultsig, encryptevid, gravlens, langstruct, quanteffects, msgcontent) are empty for roughly 30-35% of the 1,000 signal rows; these signals have simply not been assessed for the phenomenon rather than being scored as having none, so rates computed over these columns silently exclude about a third of signals.

discstat (discovery status) is empty for 32.6% of the 1,000 signal rows, meaning discovery status has not yet been determined for roughly a third of signals rather than those signals having a 'no discovery' status.
corrscore stores a signed correlation score spanning negative and positive values (examples include -0.003 and 0.001), so it behaves as a correlation coefficient rather than a non-negative magnitude.
gallat (galactic latitude) includes negative values (e.g. -0.06) as well as positive ones, consistent with positions both below and above the galactic plane.
sourcedecdeg (declination) includes negative values (e.g. -0.0312) as well as positive ones, consistent with sky positions in both northern and southern celestial hemispheres.
objradvel (radial velocity) includes both negative (e.g. -0.63) and positive (e.g. 10.85) values, consistent with sources moving toward and away from the observer.
objmetal (metallicity) includes negative values (e.g. -0.003) as well as positive ones, consistent with the standard [Fe/H]-style scale where negative values denote sub-solar metallicity.

objmag (apparent magnitude) includes negative values (e.g. -0.02) as well as positive ones, consistent with the astronomical magnitude scale where brighter objects can have lower or negative magnitudes.
doppshifthz includes both negative (e.g. -10.24) and positive (e.g. 101.96) values, consistent with signals being Doppler-shifted in either direction (approaching or receding source).
freqdrifthzs includes both negative (e.g. -0.009) and positive (e.g. 0.024) values, consistent with the signal frequency drifting either downward or upward over time.
snrratio includes negative values (e.g. -0.03) as well as positive ones, so despite its name it is not restricted to a non-negative ratio.
airtempc records sub-zero Celsius temperatures (e.g. -0.2) in addition to positive values, i.e. it is a signed temperature reading, not a magnitude.
sigclasstype classifies a signal's assessed origin into one of four values: Artificial, Natural, Candidate, or Unknown.
cultsig records a cultural-significance assessment of High or Low, and is null for 34.6% of signals where no such assessment was made.
confirmstat records the confirmation outcome of a signal's decoding as Confirmed, Rejected, or Pending.
discstat records discovery status as Full or Partial, and is null for 32.6% of signals where discovery status has not been recorded.

The business term 'technosignature probability' refers to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, the per-signal estimated likelihood that a signal originates from technology; it is distinct from biosigprob (biological-origin likelihood), natsrcprob/artsrcprob (natural vs. artificial source likelihood) and falseposprob (false-positive likelihood), which are separate scores stored in the same table.

The probability-like columns in signalprobabilities (falseposprob, techsigprob, biosigprob, natsrcprob, artsrcprob) are declared with different numeric precisions (e.g. real(5,4), real(6,2), real(7,3), real(3,1)), so they are not guaranteed to share a common 0-1 probability scale; some may be stored as percentages or bounded differently.

claims.statement: One row represents one detected signal, uniquely identified by signalregistry.
One row represents one telescope, uniquely identified by telescregistry.
One row represents one observatory/observing station, uniquely identified by observstation.
One row holds the observational conditions for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the research-process status for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds advanced-phenomena attributes for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the classification attributes for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the decoding attributes for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the dynamics attributes for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the probability scores for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.
One row holds the source-object properties for a single signal, in a one-to-one relationship with signals.

Telescopes does not cover every observatory: 48 of 963 observatories (about 5%) have no telescope row, so the absence of a telescope for a station means none was recorded, not that no instrument exists there.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks an observational-conditions record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a research-process record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks an advanced-phenomena record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a classification record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a decoding record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a dynamics record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a probability record.
This table covers all 1,000 signals present in signals; no signal lacks a source-properties record.

Observational condition dates span 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09 across 121 distinct months; dates outside this window are simply absent from the extract, and any apparent trend toward the end date is an artefact of extraction timing rather than a real decline.
A null cultsig (about 34.6% of rows) means cultural significance was not assessed or is not applicable, not that the signal has zero cultural significance.
A null discstat (about 32.6% of rows) means discovery status has not yet been determined or recorded, not that there was no discovery.
A null encryptevid (about 33.9% of rows) means encryption evidence was not evaluated, not that there is proven absence of encryption.
A null errcorrlvl (about 26.5% of rows) means the error-correction level was not recorded for that decoding attempt, not that no error correction was applied.
A null gravlens (about 33.3% of rows) means gravitational-lensing assessment was not made, not that lensing was ruled out.
A null interflvl (about 23.5% of rows) means interference level was not assessed for that signal, not that interference is absent.
A null langstruct (about 33.5% of rows) means linguistic structure was not assessed, not that no structure exists.
A null msgcontent (about 30.4% of rows) means message content was not evaluated, not that the signal is confirmed to contain no message.
A null notesmemo (about 49.2% of rows) means no free-text notes were entered, not that there is nothing noteworthy.
A null quanteffects (about 34.6% of rows) means quantum effects were not assessed, not that none were observed.
A null sigrecurr (about 33.1% of rows) means recurrence status was not assessed, not that the signal is known to be non-recurring.
airtempc stores signed Celsius temperatures and can be negative (below zero) as well as positive; it is not a magnitude-only measure.
corrscore is a signed score that can be negative or positive, centered around zero rather than bounded to [0,1] like a plain probability.
doppshifthz is signed: negative values indicate a blueshift (source approaching) and positive values a redshift (source receding), or vice versa by convention.
freqdrifthzs is signed, with negative values indicating decreasing frequency over time and positive values indicating increasing frequency.
gallat is signed galactic latitude: negative values lie south of the galactic plane and positive values lie north of it.
objmag follows the astronomical magnitude convention where values can be negative; lower (more negative) values indicate brighter objects.
objmetal is a signed metallicity value (likely dex relative to solar), where negative values indicate sub-solar metallicity.
objradvel is signed radial velocity: negative values indicate motion toward the observer and positive values motion away.
sourcedecdeg is signed declination: negative values are south of the celestial equator and positive values are north of it.
snrratio is signed and can go negative, meaning the measured signal power can fall below the noise floor rather than being a magnitude-only ratio.

"Technosignature probability" refers to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, a per-signal probability score estimating the likelihood the signal has a technological origin; it is distinct from biosigprob (biological origin), natsrcprob (natural origin) and artsrcprob (artificial-source score).

claims.statement: Each row of signals represents one distinct detected signal; signalregistry uniquely identifies that signal record.
Each row of telescopes represents one distinct telescope instrument; telescregistry uniquely identifies it.
Each row of observatories represents one distinct observing station; observstation uniquely identifies it.
Each row of observationalconditions holds the observing conditions for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of researchprocess holds the research/review status for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of signaladvancedphenomena holds the advanced-phenomena assessment for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of signalclassification holds the classification data for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of signaldecoding holds the decoding attempt data for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of signaldynamics holds the temporal/spectral stability data for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of signalprobabilities holds the probability scores for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Each row of sourceproperties holds the astrophysical source description for exactly one signal, keyed by signalref.
Every signal in signals has a validated telescope reference (telescref matches telescopes.telescregistry for all 1,000 rows), so no signal exists without a known detecting telescope in this data.

Every telescope's observstation matches a row in observatories (100% of 949 rows), so telescopes are fully contained within the recorded observatories; however because multiple telescopes can share one observatory, joining observatories to telescopes is many-to-many and will fan out, inflating any observatory-level sums.

48 of the 963 observatories (about 5%) are never referenced by any telescope, so these stations' environmental attributes exist with no linked instrument activity; an inner join from observatories to telescopes silently drops these rows.

observationalconditions only covers signals observed between 2015-02-23 and 2025-02-09 (121 distinct months); conditions for any signal observed outside this window are absent from the extract rather than zero, and an apparent trend ending at 2025-02-09 is an artefact of the extract.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in researchprocess, so this table gives complete, unduplicated research-status coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in signaladvancedphenomena, so this table gives complete, unduplicated coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in signalclassification, so this table gives complete, unduplicated classification coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in signaldecoding, so this table gives complete, unduplicated decoding coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in signaldynamics, so this table gives complete, unduplicated dynamics coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in signalprobabilities, so this table gives complete, unduplicated probability-score coverage of all signals.
Every one of the 1,000 signals in signals has exactly one matching row in sourceproperties, so this table gives complete, unduplicated source-description coverage of all signals.
cultsig records an assessed cultural-significance level (High or Low); the 34.6% of rows with no value mean the assessment was never made, not that cultural significance is known to be absent.
discstat records an assessed disclosure status (Full or Partial); the 32.6% of rows with no value mean disclosure status was never assessed, not that disclosure did not occur.
encryptevid records assessed encryption evidence (Strong or Possible); the 33.9% of rows with no value mean the evidence was never evaluated, not that encryption is confirmed absent.
errcorrlvl records an assessed error-correction level (Low, High, Medium); the 26.5% of rows with no value mean the level was never determined for that decoding attempt.
gravlens records assessed gravitational-lensing evidence (Strong or Weak); the 33.3% of rows with no value mean the assessment was never made.
interflvl records an assessed interference level (Medium, Low, High); the 23.5% of rows with no value mean interference level was never assessed for that signal, not that interference was zero.
langstruct records an assessed language structure (Complex or Simple); the 33.5% of rows with no value mean this was never assessed, not that no structure exists.
msgcontent records an assessed message-content finding (Identified or Possible); the 30.4% of rows with no value mean this was never assessed, not that no message content exists.
quanteffects records an assessed quantum-effects finding (Observed or Significant); the 34.6% of rows with no value mean this was never assessed for that signal.
sigrecurr records an assessed recurrence pattern (Regular or Sporadic); the 33.1% of rows with no value mean recurrence was never assessed, not that the signal never recurred.
notesmemo is a free-text note field; absence in 49.2% of rows means no note was recorded for that signal's research process, not that there is nothing noteworthy.
airtempc is a signed temperature in Celsius; negative values (e.g. -0.2) represent sub-zero air temperatures at the observing station.
corrscore is a signed correlation score; negative values (e.g. -0.003) indicate anti-correlation while positive values indicate positive correlation.
doppshifthz is a signed Doppler shift in Hz; negative values indicate a blue-shift (source approaching) and positive values indicate a red-shift (source receding).
freqdrifthzs is a signed drift rate in Hz/s; negative values indicate the frequency is decreasing over time and positive values indicate it is increasing.
gallat is galactic latitude in degrees; negative values indicate a position below the galactic plane and positive values indicate above it.
objmag is an astronomical magnitude where lower (including negative) values denote brighter objects; the presence of negative values reflects very bright sources, not an error.
objmetal is a metallicity index ([Fe/H]-like) relative to solar; negative values indicate sub-solar (metal-poor) composition and positive values indicate super-solar (metal-rich) composition.
objradvel is radial velocity; negative values indicate the source is approaching (blue-shifted) and positive values indicate it is receding (red-shifted).
snrratio is a signed signal-to-noise measure; negative values indicate the signal is below the noise floor and positive values indicate it is above it.
sourcedecdeg is celestial declination in degrees; negative values indicate a southern-hemisphere sky position and positive values indicate a northern one.

The business term 'technosignature probability' refers to signalprobabilities.techsigprob, the estimated probability that a signal is of technological origin; it is distinct from biosigprob (biosignature probability), natsrcprob (natural-source probability) and artsrcprob (artificial-source probability), which are separately stored probability scores.

claims.statement: One row of accountbalances represents one account-balance snapshot, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators represents one analytics-indicator snapshot, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row of marketdata represents one market-data snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats represents one market-statistics snapshot, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark.
One row of orderexecutions represents one execution/fill event, uniquely identified by orderexecmark; several executions can belong to the same order.
One row of orders represents one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot.
recordvault is the natural/business key of an order, unique per row, and is the key other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference as a foreign key.
One row of riskandmargin represents one risk/margin profile record, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row of fees represents one fee charge record, uniquely identified by feesnode.
One row of systemmonitoring represents one system-monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row of users represents one user account, uniquely identified by usersnode.
userstamp is the unique natural key of a user, referenced as a foreign key by accountbalances.usertag and orders.userlink.

The orders table holds only 733 orders, but fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin collectively reference 1,000 distinct order identifiers; 266 of those (26.6%) do not exist in orders. The orders table is therefore an incomplete subset of the full order population recorded elsewhere, and an inner join from those child tables to orders silently drops over a quarter of their rows.
267 of the 1,000 users in users have no row in orders; absence of order rows for a user means orders were not recorded for them in this table, not necessarily that they placed none.
fees contains 1,000 fee records but 26.6% of them reference an order identifier that is absent from the orders table, so fees covers charges for orders outside the current orders population.
orderexecutions contains 1,000 execution records but 26.6% of them reference an order identifier absent from the orders table, so some executions cannot be joined back to an order row.
riskandmargin contains 1,000 records but 26.6% of them reference an order identifier absent from the orders table, so some risk/margin profiles cannot be joined back to an order row.
accountbalances has exactly one balance row per user: usertag is unique and matches users.userstamp for 100% of rows, giving complete 1:1 coverage of the users table.

analyticsindicators has exactly one row per marketdata snapshot and one row per marketstats snapshot (mdataref and mstatsref are each unique and match 100%), so it fully and uniquely links the two tables.
marketstats has exactly one row per marketdata snapshot: mdlink is unique and matches marketdata.marketdatanode for 100% of rows.
systemmonitoring has exactly one row per analyticsindicators snapshot: aitrack is unique and matches analyticsindicators.analyticsindicatorsnode for 100% of rows.
walletsum (wallet balance) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum for all non-zero rows; summing walletsum together with any of its components double counts.

"Margin balance" corresponds to accountbalances.margsum, which is only one of the three components (available, frozen, margin) that sum to the wallet balance (walletsum); it is not itself the total wallet balance.
unrealline holds the unrealised profit-and-loss figure, a signed amount where positive values are unrealised gains and negative values are unrealised losses.
realline holds the realised profit-and-loss figure, a signed amount where positive values are realised gains and negative values are realised losses.
fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure, taking both positive and negative values depending on funding direction, not a strictly positive quantity.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure: positive values indicate a price increase over the day and negative values a decrease.
slipratio is a signed slippage figure, taking both positive and negative values depending on the direction of price slippage relative to the expected price.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact figure, taking both positive and negative values.
dealedge records the direction of the order, taking only the values Sell and Buy.
orderflow records an order's lifecycle status, limited to New, PartiallyFilled, and Filled; it does not include a distinct 'cancelled' status value.

"Cancelled" orders are not represented as a status in orders.orderflow; instead, cancellation is recorded separately in orderexecutions.cancelnote with reason codes Expired, InsufficientFunds, or UserRequested, and is null/empty for executions that were not cancelled.
exectune classifies a fill as Maker or Taker, and is null for about 31% of execution rows, presumably those not actually filled.
ordertune records the order type, limited to Market, Limit, Stop, and StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code, limited to GTC, GTD, FOK, and IOC.
orderbase records the channel/platform an order was placed through, limited to Web, Mobile, Bot, and API.
mktnote records the traded market/pair symbol (e.g. BTC-USD, ETH-USDT), limited to 12 distinct pairs across BTC, ETH, ADA, SOL versus USD, USDT, USDC.
feecoin records the currency a fee amount is denominated in, limited to USDT, USD, and USDC; feetotal values are not in a single common currency across rows.
feerange records a fee tier label, limited to Tier1 through Tier4.
"Trading fees" corresponds to fees.feetotal, which is recorded per fee row and denominated in whichever currency feecoin specifies (USDT, USD, or USDC) rather than a single fixed currency.
wsstate records websocket connectivity state, limited to Connected and Disconnected.
acctscope records the account type/scope, limited to Spot, Futures, Options, and Margin.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON object with multiple nested sentiment metrics (e.g. an 'instflow' field), not a single categorical or numeric value; grouping or comparing it as plain text will not correctly match equivalent sentiment profiles.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON object with multiple nested order-book depth metrics (e.g. an 'askdepth' field), not a single categorical or numeric value; grouping or comparing it as plain text will not correctly match equivalent depth profiles.

"Notional value of fills" is best read as orderexecutions.fillsum, the notional of an individual fill event, which is distinct from orders.notionsum, the notional associated with the order as a whole as originally submitted.

claims.statement: Each row of accountbalances is one account-balance snapshot record, one per user (usertag is also unique and matches users.userstamp for all rows).
Each row of analyticsindicators is one analytics-indicator snapshot, tied one-to-one to a single marketdata record (via mdataref) and a single marketstats record (via mstatsref).
Each row of fees is one fee-assessment record, linked many-to-one to an order via orderslink, though the matching order only exists in orders for 73.4% of fee rows.
Each row of marketdata is one market-data snapshot record.
Each row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, tied one-to-one to a marketdata record via mdlink.
Each row of orderexecutions is one order-execution (fill) event, linked many-to-one to an order via ordersmark, though the matching order only exists in orders for 73.4% of these rows.

Each row of orders is one order record, identified by orderspivot; recordvault is an alternate unique business key (a UUID-like code) used by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin to reference the order.
Each row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record tied to an order via ordervault, though the matching order only exists in orders for 73.4% of these rows.
Each row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, tied one-to-one to an analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
Each row of users is one user record; userstamp is the business-key identifier referenced by accountbalances and orders.

The orders table is missing roughly 26.6% of the order identifiers that fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin reference; joining those tables to orders by inner join silently drops these rows rather than indicating zero fees/fills/risk.

orders contains at most one order per user (userlink is unique across all 733 rows), so this table does not reflect users placing multiple orders; it appears to be a one-order-per-user sample rather than full order history.
267 of the 1,000 users (26.7%) are never referenced by any row in orders, so the absence of orders for a user means no order was recorded for them, not that they had no activity at all.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is not an independently observed balance, so summing walletsum together with its components double counts.
'Wallet balance' is defined as the sum of available, frozen, and margin balances (availsum + frozensum + margsum), not a separately held amount.
'Margin balance' refers to accountbalances.margsum, one of the three components (available, frozen, margin) that sum to the wallet balance.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed quantity: negative values represent unrealised losses and positive/zero values represent unrealised gains; both signs occur in the data.
realline is a signed profit/loss-style figure, with both positive and negative values occurring.
priceshiftday is a signed day-over-day price-change measure: negative values indicate a price decline and positive values indicate a price rise.
fundrate is a signed funding rate that can be negative or positive.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact metric that can be negative or positive.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio that can be negative (price moved in the trader's favor) or positive (price moved against the trader).
dealedge records the trade direction of the order: Sell or Buy.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.

claims.statement: One row is one account-balance snapshot, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode and linked to a single user via usertag.
One row is one order, uniquely identified by the surrogate key orderspivot.
recordvault is the natural business key for an order, unique per row and used by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin to reference the order.
One row is one order execution/fill (or cancellation) event tied to an order via ordersmark.
One row is one fee assessment (and any associated rebate) tied to an order via orderslink.
One row is one risk/margin profile record tied to an order via ordervault.
One row is one market-data snapshot, referenced by marketstats and analyticsindicators.
One row is one market-statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
One row is one analytics-indicator snapshot, linked to one marketdata row (mdataref) and one marketstats row (mstatsref).
One row is one system-monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row is one user, identified by the surrogate key usersnode.
userstamp is the natural business key for a user, unique per row and used by accountbalances and orders to reference the user.

The orders table does not contain every order that other tables reference: 26.6% of the rows in fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin point to a recordvault value absent from orders, so joining those tables back to orders drops roughly a quarter of their rows (orders itself holds only 733 records).
The users table includes users who never placed an order: 267 of 1,000 userstamp values have no matching row in orders.userlink, so presence in users does not imply trading activity.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it should not be summed alongside its component columns or it will double count.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed amount, with positive values representing unrealised gains and negative values representing unrealised losses.
realline is a signed amount (the realised counterpart to unrealised P&L), with both positive and negative values occurring in the data.
fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure that can be positive or negative, not a pure magnitude.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure that can be positive or negative.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio that can be positive or negative (favorable vs. unfavorable slippage).
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure that can be positive or negative.
acctscope records the account's trading venue scope, one of four categories: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.
cancelnote holds a cancellation reason code (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null/empty value (24.4% of rows) means the execution was not cancelled, not that the reason is unknown.
exectune records whether the fill was Maker or Taker liquidity; a null value (31.1% of rows) means the execution has no maker/taker classification, likely because no fill occurred.
feecoin is the currency in which the trading fee is denominated, one of USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange is a fee-tier label (Tier1 through Tier4) rather than a numeric range.
dealedge records the side of the order, Buy or Sell.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
wsstate records the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot holds a timestamp (the funding-rate snapshot time), not a numeric value, with only 8 distinct hourly timestamps observed on 2025-02-19.
market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON-formatted nested record of sentiment sub-metrics (e.g. instflow) rather than a flat categorical code, so grouping on raw substrings misrepresents the data.
quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON-formatted nested record of order-book depth sub-metrics (e.g. askdepth) rather than a flat categorical code, so grouping on raw substrings misrepresents the data.

claims.statement: The orders table holds only 733 orders, yet fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each contain 1,000 rows that reference order identifiers through orderslink/ordersmark/ordervault, and 266 of those rows (26.6%) point to order identifiers that do not exist in orders. Inner-joining fees, order executions, or risk/margin data to orders will silently drop these orders-less records, so orders is not a complete record of every order that generated a fee, execution, or risk profile.

267 of the 1,000 users in the users table are never referenced by orders.userlink, so the orders table only covers a subset (733) of registered users; absence of a user from orders means that user placed no recorded order, not that the user does not exist.
One row of accountbalances is one account-balance snapshot record, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators is one analytics-indicator record, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row of fees is one fee (and rebate) record, uniquely identified by feesnode.
One row of marketdata is one market-data (order-book depth) snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark.
One row of orderexecutions is one order-execution (fill or cancel) event, uniquely identified by orderexecmark.
One row of orders is one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot; recordvault is an alternate natural key for the same order that other tables reference.
One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row of users is one user, uniquely identified by usersnode; userstamp is an alternate natural key for the same user used by foreign keys in accountbalances and orders.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order, taking only the values Sell and Buy.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status, taking the values Filled, PartiallyFilled, and New.
ordertune records the order type, taking the values StopLimit, Stop, Market, and Limit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force instruction, taking the values GTD, FOK, GTC, and IOC.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed, taking the values Web, Mobile, Bot, and API.

cancelnote records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for the 24.4% of rows that were not cancelled, so blanks mean 'not cancelled' rather than missing data.
exectune classifies the liquidity role of an execution as Taker or Maker; it is empty for 31.1% of rows, where no fill occurred to classify.
feecoin records the currency in which the fee (and rebate) amount is denominated: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange records the fee tier applied to the trade, taking the values Tier1 through Tier4.
wsstate records the websocket connection state of the monitored session, taking the values Connected or Disconnected.
acctscope records the account/product type scope for the user, taking the values Spot, Futures, Options, and Margin.
fundspot holds a timestamp (observed values are all datetime strings), marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken.
mktnote holds the traded market/trading-pair code (e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD, BTC-USDT), one of 12 observed pair codes.

unrealline holds a signed value (both positive and negative figures occur) representing unrealised profit and loss, where negative values denote an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain.
realline holds a signed value (both positive and negative figures occur) representing realised profit and loss, where negative values denote a realised loss and positive values a realised gain.
fundrate is a signed funding rate (both positive and negative values occur), where the sign indicates the direction of the funding payment between longs and shorts, not two different kinds of data.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change (both positive and negative values occur), where the sign indicates whether price moved up or down over the day.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio (both positive and negative values occur), where the sign indicates whether execution price slipped favourably or unfavourably versus the reference price.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure (both positive and negative values occur), where the sign indicates the direction of the market effect.

walletsum (the wallet balance) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it holds in all 1,000 rows where walletsum is non-zero, so summing walletsum alongside its three components double-counts the balance.
The business term 'wallet balance' refers to the full walletsum total (available + frozen + margin), not to any single component such as available or margin funds alone.
'Margin balance' corresponds to margsum, which is only one of the three components summed into walletsum (wallet balance); it is not the user's total wallet balance.

'Unrealised profit and loss' corresponds to accountbalances.unrealline, which can be negative (a loss) or positive (a gain), and is a separate figure from realised P&L (realline) and from the wallet/margin balances.
'Trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal, the gross fee charged per fill; any rebate given back (rebtotal) is a separate, offsetting amount and is not included in feetotal.
'Notional value of fills' corresponds to orderexecutions.fillsum, the value of an individual execution/fill, which is distinct from orders.notionsum, the notional value recorded for the whole order.

One row represents one market data snapshot.

One row represents one risk/margin profile record, optionally associated with one order via ordervault.

Fees, order executions and risk/margin records reference order identifiers (such as 'OB101796') that do not exist in orders for 26.6% of their rows, meaning the orders table omits roughly a quarter of the orders that otherwise have fee, execution, or risk data recorded.
26.6% of fee records reference an order identifier not present in the orders table, so joining fees to orders will silently drop these rows and understate total fees per order.
26.6% of order execution records reference an order identifier not present in the orders table, so joining executions to orders will silently drop these rows.
26.6% of risk/margin records reference an order identifier not present in the orders table, so joining risk/margin data to orders will silently drop these rows.

dealedge records the trade side of the order: Buy or Sell.

feecoin holds the currency the fee was denominated in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange holds the fee tier label applied to the transaction: Tier1, Tier2, Tier3, or Tier4.

claims.statement: Each row of orders is one order; orderspivot (and equivalently recordvault) uniquely identifies it.
Each row of accountbalances is one account balance snapshot, and the table holds exactly one such row per user since usertag is also unique and matches users one-to-one.
Each row of fees is one fee charge record, usually tied to a single order via orderslink.
Each row of orderexecutions is one execution/fill event, usually tied to a single order via ordersmark.
Each row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record, usually tied to a single order via ordervault.
Each row of marketdata is one market data snapshot.
Each row of marketstats is one market statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a single marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
Each row of analyticsindicators is one analytics indicator snapshot, linked one-to-one to both a marketdata record (mdataref) and a marketstats record (mstatsref).
Each row of systemmonitoring is one monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to a single analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
Each row of users is one user, identified by usersnode/userstamp.

Orders only covers the subset of users who actually placed an order (733 of 1,000 users); the other 267 users have no order history recorded here, which means 'no order recorded', not necessarily 'never traded'.

26.6% of fees rows reference an order id that does not exist in the orders table, so fee records exist for orders that fall outside the current orders snapshot; joining fees to orders will silently drop these.

26.6% of orderexecutions rows reference an order id that does not exist in the orders table, so execution/fill records exist for orders outside the current orders snapshot; joining to orders will silently drop these.

26.6% of riskandmargin rows reference an order id that does not exist in the orders table, so risk/margin profiles exist for orders outside the current orders snapshot; joining to orders will silently drop these.
accountbalances has full one-to-one coverage of users: every one of the 1,000 account balance rows matches a user, and there is exactly one row per user.
marketdata has no foreign key to orders or users; its snapshots are market-wide and cannot be scoped to a particular trader or order.
systemmonitoring has no foreign key to orders or users; its rows are system-level snapshots not scoped to a particular trader or order.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it holds for all 1,000 non-zero rows, so summing walletsum alongside its components double counts.
margsum is the margin-allocated component of a user's wallet balance, distinct from available (availsum) and frozen (frozensum) funds.

unrealline is a signed quantity: negative values denote an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain; the two 'format classes' found are simply negative vs. positive numbers, not two different kinds of values.
realline is a signed quantity: negative values denote a realised loss and positive values a realised gain; the two 'format classes' found are simply negative vs. positive numbers.

priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure: negative values indicate a price decline and positive values an increase; the 'format classes' reported are an artifact of the minus sign, not distinct kinds of data.
fundrate is a signed funding rate that can be negative or positive; the two 'format classes' reported are an artifact of the minus sign, not distinct kinds of data.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact metric, with negative and positive values; the two 'format classes' reported are an artifact of the minus sign, not distinct kinds of data.

slipratio is a signed slippage ratio, with negative and positive values indicating the direction of execution slippage; the two 'format classes' reported are an artifact of the minus sign, not distinct kinds of data.
cancelnote is empty for 24.4% of rows, meaning the execution was not cancelled; non-null values give the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested).
exectune is empty for 31.1% of rows, meaning no maker/taker classification was recorded for that execution; non-null values are Taker or Maker.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON document of nested sentiment metrics (e.g. instflow) rather than a flat category code; many raw string values are near-duplicate floating-point variants of the same underlying reading, so grouping on the raw text over-splits the data.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON document of quote book depth (e.g. askdepth) rather than a flat category code; many raw string values are near-duplicate variants of the same underlying reading, so grouping on the raw text over-splits the data.
acctscope holds four account-type categories: Spot, Futures, Options, Margin, roughly evenly distributed.
dealedge is a Buy/Sell direction flag for the order.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, or Filled.
feecoin is the currency the fee was charged in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange is a fee-tier label (Tier1 through Tier4).
'Wallet balance' means the total of available, frozen, and margin sums (walletsum = availsum + frozensum + margsum), not just the spendable or available cash.
'Margin balance' is best represented by margsum, the margin-allocated portion of a user's wallet balance, which is only part of (not equal to) the total wallet balance.
'Unrealised profit and loss' refers to unrealline, which is distinct from realised profit and loss (realline) and can be negative (loss) or positive (gain).

'Trading fees' is stored as fees.feetotal, but 26.6% of fee rows cannot be tied back to a corresponding order in the orders table, so a fee-to-order join will understate fee totals attributable to recorded orders.

'Notional value of fills' is best represented by orderexecutions.fillsum, the dollar value actually filled per execution, which is distinct from orders.notionsum, the notional of the order as originally placed (which may exceed what was actually filled).

'Holdings' most plausibly corresponds to marketstats.mkthold, a market-level holdings figure, rather than to any per-user balance column; no column in accountbalances is explicitly named for holdings.

claims.statement: Each row of accountbalances is one balance snapshot for a single user; accountbalancesnode is the surrogate key and usertag is a one-to-one business key to users.userstamp.
Each row of users represents one user account; userstamp is the unique business identifier used as the join key from accountbalances and orders.
Each row of orders represents one order placed by a user; orderspivot is the surrogate primary key.
recordvault is the unique business identifier of an order and is the key referenced by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin.
Each row of fees is one fee assessment record, generally tied to a single order via orderslink.
Each row of orderexecutions is one execution, fill, or cancellation event associated with an order via ordersmark.
Each row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile snapshot tied to a single order via ordervault.
Each row of marketdata is one market quote-depth snapshot.
Each row of marketstats is one market statistics snapshot, in one-to-one correspondence with a marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
Each row of analyticsindicators is one analytics snapshot, in one-to-one correspondence with both a marketdata snapshot (mdataref) and a marketstats snapshot (mstatsref).
Each row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, in one-to-one correspondence with an analyticsindicators snapshot via aitrack.

The orders table holds only 733 order records, while fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each contain 1,000 rows and reference order identifiers missing from orders in 266 cases (26.6%); orders does not cover the full population of orders implied by its child tables, and joins from those tables will silently drop about a quarter of their rows.

267 of the 1,000 users in users are never referenced by orders.userlink, so orders covers only about 73% of registered users; absence of an order for a user reflects no recorded order rather than no activity, since accountbalances covers all 1,000 users.

In this dataset every order belongs to a distinct user (userlink has 733 distinct values across the 733 order rows), so the orders table captures at most one order per user rather than a full order history per user.

fees contains 1,000 rows but only 73.4% have a matching order in orders; the remaining 266 rows (26.6%) point to order identifiers absent from orders, so fee records exist for orders not present in this orders table.

orderexecutions contains 1,000 rows but only 73.4% have a matching order in orders; the remaining 266 rows (26.6%) point to order identifiers absent from orders, so execution/fill records exist for orders not present in this orders table.

riskandmargin contains 1,000 rows but only 73.4% have a matching order in orders; the remaining 266 rows (26.6%) point to order identifiers absent from orders, so risk/margin profile records exist for orders not present in this orders table.

marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators, and systemmonitoring form a self-contained one-to-one chain of 1,000 snapshots with no foreign key to orders or users, so none of this market, analytics, or monitoring data can be attributed to a specific order or user.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is not an independently recorded balance, so summing walletsum together with its components double counts.
realline holds both positive and negative values, consistent with a realized profit-and-loss figure where sign indicates gain versus loss.
unrealline holds both positive and negative values, consistent with unrealized profit-and-loss where sign indicates unrealized gain versus loss.
priceshiftday holds both positive and negative values, representing the daily price change where the sign indicates a decline or an increase.
fundrate holds both positive and negative values, consistent with a funding rate where sign indicates the direction of payment between long and short positions.
slipratio holds both positive and negative values, consistent with a slippage measure where sign indicates whether execution was worse or better than expected.
mkteffect holds both positive and negative values, consistent with a market-impact measure where sign indicates the direction of the price effect.
dealedge holds exactly two values, Buy and Sell, denoting the trade direction of the order.
orderflow holds three values (New, PartiallyFilled, Filled) denoting the lifecycle status of an order.
ordertune holds four values (StopLimit, Stop, Market, Limit) denoting the order type.
timespan holds four values (GTD, FOK, GTC, IOC) denoting the order's time-in-force instruction.
orderbase holds four values (Web, Mobile, Bot, API) denoting the channel or platform through which the order was placed.
feerange holds four tier labels (Tier1 through Tier4) denoting the fee-rate bracket applied to the transaction.
feecoin holds three stablecoin values (USDT, USD, USDC) denoting the currency in which the fee was charged.
cancelnote holds Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested, or null; a null value (24.4% of rows) means the execution was never cancelled rather than data being missing.
exectune holds Taker, Maker, or null; a null value (31.1% of rows) means no maker/taker role has been assigned, consistent with an execution event that has not been filled.
wsstate holds Connected or Disconnected, denoting the websocket connection state at the time of the monitoring snapshot.
acctscope holds Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin, denoting the trading account type or scope of the user.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON-structured value (e.g. a 'flow.instflow' metric) bundling multiple sentiment sub-metrics into one text field rather than a single scalar category; grouping on the raw text undercounts the true number of distinct metric combinations.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON-structured value (e.g. a 'depth.askdepth' metric) bundling multiple order-book depth sub-metrics into one text field rather than a single scalar category; grouping on the raw text undercounts the true number of distinct metric combinations.
'Wallet balance' refers to accountbalances.walletsum, which is defined as the sum of availsum, frozensum, and margsum rather than an independently stored total.
'Margin balance' corresponds to accountbalances.margsum, one of the three components summed into walletsum, rather than the whole wallet balance.
'Unrealised profit and loss' corresponds to accountbalances.unrealline, whose sign indicates an unrealized gain (positive) or loss (negative).
'Trading fees' corresponds to fees.feetotal, the total fee amount recorded per fee record; rebtotal is a separate rebate amount, not included in feetotal.
'Notional value of fills' corresponds to orderexecutions.fillsum, the notional amount of an individual fill event, distinct from orders.notionsum which is the notional value of the order as a whole.
