claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance snapshot for a single user (via usertag), identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row represents one set of market-sentiment analytics tied to a single marketdata record and a single marketstats record, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row represents one fee (and any associated rebate) record linked to a single order, identified by feesnode.
One row represents one market-depth/quote snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot linked to a marketdata record, identified by marketstatsmark.
One row represents one fill/execution event tied to an order, identified by orderexecmark.
One row represents one order; orderspivot is the surrogate key and recordvault is the unique business key referenced by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin.
One row represents one risk/margin profile tied to a single order, identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot linked to an analyticsindicators record, identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row represents one user account, identified by usersnode (with userstamp as the natural key referenced by other tables).

The orders table holds only 733 order records even though fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each contain 1,000 rows and about 26.6% of those rows point to order identifiers not present in orders; orders is therefore a partial extract that silently omits roughly 267 orders that still have associated fee, execution, and risk records elsewhere.
About 26.6% of fee rows reference an order (via orderslink) that does not exist in the orders table, so an inner join from fees to orders will silently drop these rows.
About 26.6% of execution rows reference an order (via ordersmark) that does not exist in the orders table, so an inner join from orderexecutions to orders will silently drop these rows.
About 26.6% of risk/margin rows reference an order (via ordervault) that does not exist in the orders table, so an inner join from riskandmargin to orders will silently drop these rows.
267 of the 1,000 users are never referenced by any order; the absence of order rows for them means no order was recorded for that user in this data, not necessarily that the user never traded.
dealedge records the trade side as Sell or Buy.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status, limited to Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New in this data; no Cancelled or Rejected status appears here.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, GTC, or IOC.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
exectune records the execution role, Maker or Taker; a null value (31.1% of rows) means the role is not applicable, likely because the order was not matched/filled.
cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null value (24.4% of rows) means the order was not cancelled.
feerange records a fee tier label (Tier1-Tier4), likely a volume- or account-based fee bracket.
feecoin records the currency in which the fee amount is denominated: USDT, USD, or USDC.
wsstate records the websocket connection state of the monitored session: Connected or Disconnected.
acctscope records the account's trading scope/segment: Spot, Futures, Options, or Margin.
fundspot stores a date-time stamp (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46'), not a price or spot value despite its name; it marks when the funding-rate snapshot was taken.
realline holds signed values (both positive and negative) representing realized profit/loss; the sign indicates gain versus loss rather than the column holding two kinds of identifiers.
unrealline holds signed values (both positive and negative) representing unrealized profit/loss; the sign indicates an open gain versus an open loss.
priceshiftday holds signed values representing the day's price change direction (increase or decrease), not two distinct identifier formats.
fundrate holds signed values representing the direction of the funding payment (positive or negative funding rate), not two distinct identifier formats.
mkteffect holds signed values representing the direction of market impact (positive or negative effect), not two distinct identifier formats.
slipratio holds signed values representing slippage direction (favorable versus unfavorable), not two distinct identifier formats.
walletsum is derived as availsum + frozensum + margsum; it is not an independent balance and summing it together with its components double counts.
'Wallet balance' corresponds to walletsum and is the sum of a user's available, frozen, and margin sub-balances combined, not just liquid/spendable cash.
'Margin balance' corresponds to margsum, the margin-committed portion of a user's wallet balance, and excludes the available and frozen sub-balances.
'Unrealised profit and loss' corresponds to unrealline, distinct from realized P&L (realline); its signed value indicates an open gain (positive) or loss (negative).
'Trading fees' corresponds to fees.feetotal, the gross fee amount charged on an order; it is distinct from rebtotal, which records a separate rebate rather than being netted into feetotal.

'Notional value of fills' corresponds to orderexecutions.fillsum, recorded at the execution/fill grain, and is distinct from orders.notionsum which is the order's originally requested notional at the order grain; only orders whose recordvault matches an orderexecutions.ordersmark (about 73.4% of fee/execution rows) have a linked fill notional.
